464	- **Minors folded in:**
465	  - the full gate list (§ 7);
466	  - `deny_unknown_fields` (D26);
467	  - stream-level handling of oversized records (D8);
468	  - `Cow` / `RawValue` skeletons (§ 5.1);
469	  - the non-stream order and billing (§ 5.2);
470	  - the held trailing CR (D2);
471	  - the `Other` payload (§ 4.1);
472	  - `name_sha256_8` (§ 4.6);
473	  - the SDK `mapError` mapping (§ 7).
474	- **Questions, answered:**
475	  - Observe mode is specified in § 5.3.
476	  - The decider is called once per completed hold. SMA-753 orders by completion.
477	  - The SDK targets are pinned in § 8.2. Canonical form makes the SDKs agree.
478	  - The capability is not exposed (D28).
479	  - The caller is not an adversary (T3), which leaves request-side differentials to SMA-752.
480	
481	## 11. Implementation rulings (2026-11-11)
482	
483	The controller made these rulings during implementation. Each one changes or settles
484	behaviour that §§ 3–6 left open, and each fails closed. The sentences they made stale are
485	edited in place above (D12's reason, § 4.3, § 4.4, § 5.2).
486	
487	**OpenAI classification and canonical form.**
488	
489	- **`choice_order` (P-10 (a)).** A choice index seen for the first time must equal the number
490	  of choices seen so far, or the record is `Deviation("choice_order")`. openai-python finds a
491	  stream choice by list position, so choice 1 before choice 0 would merge two choices' calls.
492	- **Choice-0-only tool data.** A tool-call fragment (`tool_calls` or `function_call`) in a
493	  choice whose `index` is not 0 is `Deviation("multi_choice_tool_calls")`. Tool data in a
494	  choice entry at array position other than 0 of its chunk is `Deviation("choice_position")`.
495	  LangChain reads `choices[0]` of each chunk and ignores `choice.index`. **Limitation:** an
496	  `n > 1` request whose later choices call tools is not supported while interception is on. It
497	  gets `on_failure` (block, or pass-through in observe mode). The non-stream body applies the
498	  same rules, as `Malformed`.
499	- **Duplicate choice index.** A chunk that names one choice index twice is
500	  `Malformed("duplicate_choice_index")`.
501	- **The `object` rule.** Stream: a chunk that carries tool data or a `finish_reason` must have
502	  `object` exactly `"chat.completion.chunk"`, or it is `Malformed("object")`; openai-python
503	  skips any other chunk. Body: `object` must be `"chat.completion"` only when the body carries
504	  tool calls.
505	- **`type_shape_mismatch`.** A `type` that disagrees with the entry's body shape (`function` or
506	  `custom`) is a deviation, never kind `Other`: clients ignore `type` and run the body. Kind
507	  `Other` applies only when no `function` or `custom` body arrived.
508	- **`incomplete_arguments`.** At completion, OpenAI function and legacy-function arguments
509	  (stream and body) must be `""` or one complete JSON value; Anthropic `tool_use` input at
510	  `content_block_stop` the same. Otherwise the call is `Deviation("incomplete_arguments")`
511	  (`Malformed` in a body). `""` is presented to the decider as `"{}"`. Custom-tool input is
512	  free text and is not checked. Reason: LangChain and anthropic-python partial-parse truncated
513	  JSON, so the decider would see different arguments than the client runs.
514	- **`long_identifier`.** A tool-call id or name over 1024 bytes is `Deviation("long_identifier")`
515	  (`Malformed` in a body), in both protocols: OpenAI at the phase-1 check, Anthropic at
516	  `content_block_start` for `tool_use`, server and other blocks. Real ids and names are under
517	  100 bytes. A completed block keeps its name for the stream's life, so up to 4096 blocks of
518	  near-record-cap names would be retained outside held-byte accounting. A completed Anthropic
519	  block also moves its id out instead of cloning it.
520	- **`second_finish`.** A second `finish_reason` for one choice is a deviation, for tool-free
521	  choices too.
522	- **Arguments may be `null`** in a fragment (§ 4.3). It adds nothing, as in every SDK.
523	- **P-10 (b), never drop.** The rewrite never removes a choice entry and never drops a frame
524	  (§ 4.4), so the gateway's own rewrite cannot shift openai-python's positions.
525	- **Notice meta.** A notice chunk copies `id`, `created`, `model` and `system_fingerprint` only
526	  when they are strings or numbers, and always says `"object":"chat.completion.chunk"`. Only
527	  accepted records update the meta that the closing notice uses, so a dropped record cannot
528	  name it.
529	- **Prior OpenAI calls.** A request's prior assistant `tool_calls` entry reads `function.name`
530	  and `function.arguments`, or `custom.name` and `custom.input`. An entry with neither body,
531	  with both, or with a body that disagrees with its `type` makes the turn
532	  `Unavailable("malformed")`, as a `function` without a `name` does (D19).
533	
534	**Anthropic.**
535	
536	- **`block_interleave`.** A `content_block_start` while an earlier block is still open is a
537	  deviation. LangChain routes `input_json_delta` to the most recent start, not to
538	  `event.index`.
539	- **Synthesized stop frame.** A blocked block's `content_block_stop` is re-emitted as the
540	  synthesized `{"type":"content_block_stop","index":i}`, never the upstream payload.
541	
542	**Bodies and numbers.**
543	
544	- **`lossy_number`.** A body (either format) holding a number outside `u64`/`i64` that is an
545	  integral `f64` with magnitude of 2^53 or more is `Malformed("lossy_number")`. serde_json would
546	  round it, and the decider would see a different number than the client. The rule applies to
547	  stream kind-Other calls too, in both protocols: their arguments are the parsed raw entries, so
548	  a raw entry holding such a number makes the call's completion `Deviation("lossy_number")`.
549	- **`preserve_order`.** `paigasus-gateway-core` enables serde_json's `preserve_order`, so a
550	  re-serialized frame or body keeps the upstream key order in every build.
551	
552	**Strict JSON scope (I-1).** The D5 envelope rules (case-folded classifier keys, `constructor`,
553	`prototype`) apply to envelope keys only. Tool argument and schema data gets JSON validity,
554	duplicate-key rejection at every depth, non-finite rejection and `__proto__` rejection, but not
555	the case-fold or `constructor`/`prototype` checks: the classifiers never read inside it, and a
556	tool may take an argument named `Id` or `constructor`. That data is OpenAI function and legacy
557	arguments, Anthropic `tool_use` and `server_tool_use` `input`, a request's
558	`tools[].function.parameters` and `functions[].parameters`, an Anthropic request's
559	`tools[].input_schema`, and prior-call inputs in the request. In a whole-record, body or
560	request parse, the value of an `input`, `parameters` or `input_schema` key gets these rules.
561	
562	**Interceptor and limits.**
563	
564	- **Wrong-length decision vectors.** A decision vector whose length differs from the calls'
565	  blocks every call of the hold with `DeciderError` (stream and body), not only the missing ones.
566	- **`after_done` before `oversized`.** After `[DONE]` (or `message_stop`) every record is
567	  dropped and counted as `after_done`, an oversized one included. It never becomes a stream
568	  failure.
569	- **Oversized records** are always dropped and counted with the new `records_dropped` reason
570	  `oversized` (§ 5.2), in both `on_failure` modes (P-3). With `allow` the stream then switches
571	  to pass-through.
572	- **Observed holds are bounded (D13).** A hold under observe mode (§ 5.3) keeps assembling for
573	  the report, but once it retains more than `max_held_bytes` of arguments and raw entries it
574	  drops them and is never decided: no decision and no report entry, as for a pass-through
575	  call. Its frames still flow. A completed hold keeps no arguments in either protocol.
576	- **86 400 s caps.** Every `[tool_interception]` `*_secs` value is capped at 86 400 by
577	  validation; `Instant + Duration` would otherwise panic on overflow.
578

# SMA-749 — gateway: assemble, hold and rewrite tool calls in the response path

- Linear: SMA-749 (spec 1 of the SMA-747 umbrella, "Gateway tool-call interception").
- ADR: ADR-0027 (Accepted 2026-11-08), decisions (a) one check point, (b) hold only tool
  calls, (c) replace a blocked call with a notice, (e) evaluation in the gateway.
- Status: approved on 2026-11-09, after the spec challenge (§ 10).
- Amended 2026-11-11: the implementation rulings are recorded in § 11, and the sentences they
  changed are edited in place.
- Scope: a new lib crate `paigasus-gateway-core` (a synchronous, I/O-free state machine), and
  its wiring into `paigasus-gateway`'s `/v1/chat/completions` handler, off by default.
- Out of scope: the policy decision itself (SMA-752), session history (SMA-753), detectors
  (SMA-754), the decision log (SMA-755), the Anthropic ingress route (SMA-750), MCP (SMA-756),
  any rewrite of the request body, and the non-goals in § 2.

## 1. Problem

The gateway forwards model responses byte for byte. A response can contain tool calls: the
model asks the client's agent to run a function with some arguments. Today nothing between the
model and the client can look at a tool call, decide on it, or remove it.

ADR-0027 puts that check in the gateway. Every later spec needs the same foundation first:

1. find every tool call in a response, streaming or not, for OpenAI Chat Completions and
   Anthropic Messages;
2. hold a streaming tool call until it is complete, while text keeps streaming;
3. ask a decider about the complete calls;
4. forward allowed calls and replace blocked ones with a notice, in a response the client's
   SDK still parses.

This spec builds that foundation with a decider that allows everything. It ships wired in and
off by default.

## 2. Threat model and invariant

**Adversaries.**

- T1. **Model output is hostile**, always. Prompt injection can make the model emit any tool
  call, any arguments, any text.
- T2. **The upstream may be non-conforming or compromised.** `upstream.openai.base_url` and
  `extra_ca_bundle_path` exist for self-hosted vLLM / LiteLLM (SMA-558). Such upstreams
  interleave indices, emit odd framing, or can be made to emit arbitrary bytes. Nothing about
  the upstream's framing or JSON is trusted.
- T3. **The caller is not an adversary of its own agent** in this spec. Request-side
  differentials (for example duplicate `tools` keys) are SMA-752's concern.

**Invariant (I1).** For every supported client parser P (§ 8.2), every tool call that P
accumulates from the bytes the gateway emits was decided `Allow`, with the same choice, kind,
name and arguments that the decider saw. Anything the gateway cannot classify with certainty
is not forwarded (or triggers `on_failure`).

**Non-goals.** Tool calls encoded inside text content (ReAct / XML conventions, or a vLLM tool
parser that fails and falls back to `content`); tools executed by the provider (Anthropic
`server_tool_use`, `mcp_tool_use`); the OpenAI Responses API; request rewriting.

## 3. Decisions

| Id | Question | Decision |
|----|----------|----------|
| D1 | Where the code lives | New crate `paigasus-gateway-core` (`publish = false`): types, SSE framing, JSON classification, assembly, rewrite, as a sans-IO state machine. `paigasus-gateway` drives it with tokio. No kernel change in this spec. |
| D2 | SSE input framing | WHATWG line splitting (CR, LF, CRLF), with a CR held until the next byte. Strip one leading UTF-8 BOM. Multi-line `data:` joined with `\n`. |
| D3 | SSE output framing | **Re-framed, not forwarded.** For every classified record, emit `data: <original payload bytes>\n\n` (Anthropic: preceded by `event: <validated name>\n`). Upstream comments, `id:`, `retry:` and unknown fields are dropped. |
| D4 | End of stream | An unterminated last record is parsed and classified (as `UsageScanner::finish` does). Records after `[DONE]` are dropped and counted. |
| D5 | JSON parsing | One strict parse for stream records and non-stream bodies. A record is **malformed** if it is not valid JSON, has a duplicate key at any depth, has a `__proto__` / `constructor` / `prototype` key, or has a key that case-folds to a classifier key without being byte-equal to it. |
| D6 | Frame classification | Total, by a positive allowlist (§ 4.2): **tool-free** (forward), **tool-bearing** (hold), **malformed** (D7). Nothing else. |
| D7 | A malformed record | Queue empty: dropped and counted (never forwarded). Queue non-empty: `on_failure` for the whole stream. |
| D8 | Records over `max_record_bytes` | Never skipped. Stream-level `on_failure` (the choice cannot be known without parsing). |
| D9 | Canonical assembly | Strict rules (§ 4.3). Any deviation is `on_failure` for the stream. Where client SDK accumulators disagree, the strict form makes them agree. |
| D10 | When a hold completes (OpenAI) | At its choice's `finish_reason`. `[DONE]` or EOF with an open hold and no `finish_reason` = truncated → `on_failure`, never "complete". |
| D11 | When a hold completes (Anthropic) | At `content_block_stop` of the block. `message_stop` / EOF with an open block = truncated → `on_failure`. |
| D12 | Ordering and release | **One FIFO per stream.** Once any hold is open, every later frame is queued in order. Each queued frame carries the set of (choice, call) or (block) it touches. A frame is releasable when every member of its set is decided. Release pops from the head and stops at the first frame that is not releasable. Text before the first hold is forwarded at once. |
| D13 | Held memory | `max_held_bytes` (default 4 MiB) is a **per-stream total** of the queue. Overflow → `on_failure` for every open hold. |
| D14 | Time limits | `max_hold_secs` (default 300, equal to `stream_idle_timeout_secs`) from a hold's first frame to its completion; `decide_timeout_secs` (default 5) for the decider. Either → `on_failure` for that hold. |
| D15 | Keep-alive | `: keep-alive\n\n` every `keepalive_secs` (default 10) while the queue is non-empty and nothing else was emitted. |
| D16 | `on_failure` | `"block"` (default) or `"allow"` (observe mode, § 5.3). |
| D17 | Upstream transport error | The state machine consumes `Result<Bytes, _>`. On `Err` it is aborted: the queue is dropped, then the existing `TERMINAL_SSE_ERROR` is emitted. An upstream `{"error":…}` record while a hold is open is treated the same. |
| D18 | Decider contract | `decide(ctx: Arc<DecisionContext>, turn: Arc<ToolTurn>, calls: Vec<ToolCall>) -> BoxFuture<'static, Result<Vec<Decision>, DeciderError>>`. Called once per completed hold. A result whose length differs from `calls.len()` is a `DeciderError`. Release looks up each call's decision; a missing one is `Block`. |
| D19 | Request side | Parse the request into `ToolTurn::Parsed { definitions, prior_calls, tool_results }`, including legacy `functions` and `role:"function"` messages. A parse failure gives `ToolTurn::Unavailable(reason)`, never an empty `Parsed`. No request rewrite. |
| D20 | Rewrite rules | § 4.4. Blocked calls are removed per fragment; `role` is always kept; `logprobs` are stripped from rewritten frames; `finish_reason` / `stop_reason` are rewritten wherever they arrive, including after a hold closed by `on_failure`. |
| D21 | Notice | Fixed text built from `BlockCode` and a sanitized name; never from argument or detector content (§ 4.5). |
| D22 | Decision reporting | Streaming: `: paigasus-decision <ASCII-escaped JSON>` per decision, emitted just before the frames that hold released. Non-stream: `paigasus-tool-decisions` header, ASCII-escaped JSON, capped at 2 KiB with `"truncated":true`. Schema in § 4.6. |
| D23 | Identity | With `AllowAll`, the sequence of emitted `data` payloads is byte-equal to the upstream's classified payloads; only gateway comments are added. Framing may differ (D3). |
| D24 | Billing | `UsageScanner` and `ChargeGuard` keep reading the raw upstream bytes before the state machine; `non_stream_usage` reads the original body. A drop, a rewrite or the new 502 does not change the charge. |
| D25 | Cancellation | Nothing is spawned. The decider future is owned by the relay's stream state. Client disconnect drops everything, as today. |
| D26 | Config | `[tool_interception]`, `#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]`, `enabled = false`. Only `/v1/chat/completions` is wired. Anthropic is library code until SMA-750. |
| D27 | Interception off | The relay is exactly today's relay. The state machine is not constructed. |
| D28 | Capability exposure | Not advertised in `service_info` in this spec. It reveals security posture and has no consumer yet. |
| D29 | Property testing | `proptest` with grammar-based generators against a differential oracle (§ 8.1), not `cargo-fuzz` (stable 1.95 pin; `cargo-fuzz` needs nightly). |

### Reasons

- **D1, no kernel change.** The challenge found that `paigasus-kernel` is `publish = true` and
  tied by `repo:version-lockstep` to the py and npm binding releases. Types no binding exports
  would still force a kernel release. ADR-0027 (e) places evaluation in the gateway via the
  kernel's `decide()`, which arrives with Cedar in SMA-752. The shared types move to the kernel
  then, when they have a binding user. Until then they live in gateway-core with
  `#[non_exhaustive]`. `DecisionId` is deferred to SMA-755, its only user.
- **D1, sans-IO.** A runtime-free `Stream` that polls the upstream, a decider future and two
  timers at once is the hardest shape to get right and to test. A synchronous machine with
  explicit inputs and actions makes the properties in § 8 plain synchronous tests, and it
  removes the self-referential-future problem of a borrowed decider call.
- **D3, re-framing.** Any byte the gateway forwards without reading is a channel to a client
  that reads it differently: a BOM-prefixed first line (`TextDecoder` strips the BOM, this
  repo's own `chat-stream.ts` and `paigasus-sdk/src/chat.ts` use it), lax line-trimming
  clients (`paigasus-sdk/src/chat.ts:108` trims), records after `[DONE]`, a JSON body
  returned on a `stream:true` request. Re-framing closes the whole class. Payload bytes stay
  untouched, so D23 still catches any accidental re-serialization.
- **D5, strict JSON.** Records that parse everywhere but mean different things are worse than
  records that fail. Duplicate keys: serde and JS keep the last, Go's `encoding/json` merges
  struct-typed duplicates. Case-insensitive matching in Go and Newtonsoft makes
  `"Tool_Calls"` a tool call to them. `__proto__` can change the accumulated object in
  JavaScript. Rejecting all of these costs nothing on a conforming upstream.
- **D6, positive allowlist.** "Has a `tool_calls` key" is wrong both ways. It misses
  `tool_calls` as an object or string and `message.tool_calls` inside a chunk. It also holds
  all text on upstreams that send `"tool_calls": []` on every delta (some vLLM versions).
- **D9, canonical assembly.** The SDKs disagree. openai-python concatenates every string field
  except `index` and `type`, so a second `name` fragment becomes `safe_` + `rm`. openai-node
  replaces it. anthropic-python appends a block on start but applies deltas by index. The
  decider must see what every client will run, and that is only knowable for the canonical
  form.
- **D10/D11, truncation.** The relay turns a transport error into a data record and a clean
  end. An assembler placed after that conversion would see EOF and release a call cut off
  mid-arguments. D17 moves the state machine in front of the conversion.
- **D12, one FIFO.** Per-choice holds with a shared tail leak: releasing hold A would ship
  frames of hold B sitting in A's tail. A frame can also carry several choices. Keeping the
  stream order and releasing only fully decided frames is the simplest rule that never leaks.
  The cost: other choices pause during a hold. Interception supports tool calls in choice 0
  only (§ 11), so an `n > 1` request whose later choices call tools is not supported while
  interception is on.
- **D13, per-stream total.** `n` is caller-controlled (up to 128 on OpenAI). A per-hold cap
  multiplies by `n`.
- **D14, 300 s.** A file-writing call with 40 KB of arguments takes about 200 s at 50 tok/s. A
  60 s cap would block it. The decider timeout is separate because SMA-752 may add a remote
  call.
- **D18, owned arguments and length check.** A future decider that returns too few decisions
  must not silently allow the rest. `DecisionContext` carries the caller (principal, scope,
  org) and the request ids, captured in the handler. Inside the stream, `current_ids()` is
  `None` (SMA-504 §4.3).
- **D19, `Unavailable`.** An empty `Parsed` would make SMA-753's sequence rules fail open on a
  request that did not parse.
- **D21, closed notice text.** The model reads the notice on its next turn. Echoing detector
  or argument content would reflect attacker text into the prompt.
- **D22, header cap.** Many parallel calls can exceed nginx's default 4–8 KiB
  `proxy_buffer_size`, and the proxy would turn the response into a 502. `HeaderValue`
  rejects raw UTF-8.
- **D24, billing.** The upstream produced and billed the tokens of a blocked call. The charge
  follows the upstream, as SMA-677 and SMA-730 decided.

## 4. Semantics

### 4.1 Types (`paigasus-gateway-core::types`, all `#[non_exhaustive]`)

```rust
pub enum ToolCallKind { Function, Custom, LegacyFunctionCall, AnthropicToolUse, Other }

pub struct ToolCall {
    pub choice: u32,              // OpenAI choice index; 0 for Anthropic
    pub position: u32,            // tool-call index (OpenAI) or block index (Anthropic)
    pub id: Option<String>,       // absent for legacy function_call
    pub name: String,
    pub kind: ToolCallKind,
    pub arguments: String,        // see below
}

pub enum Decision { Allow, Block { code: BlockCode } }
pub enum BlockCode { Policy, Detector, HoldLimit, Malformed, Truncated, DeciderError }
pub enum Basis { Decider, OnFailure }   // how a decision was reached (§ 5.3)
```

`arguments` holds: the concatenated `function.arguments` string (Function, LegacyFunctionCall);
`custom.input` (Custom); the concatenated `partial_json` (AnthropicToolUse); the raw JSON of the
whole tool-call entry (Other).

### 4.2 Classification

**OpenAI stream chunk.** Tool-free if all of these hold:

- the payload is a JSON object, and `choices` is absent or an array of objects;
- every `choices[i].index` is a JSON integer literal in `0..=127`;
- every `delta` is absent or an object, and no choice has a `message` key;
- every `delta.tool_calls` is absent, `null` or `[]`, and every `delta.function_call` is
  absent or `null`.

Tool-bearing if the above holds except that some `delta.tool_calls` is a non-empty array of
objects, or some `delta.function_call` is an object. Anything else is malformed.

`{"error":…}` at the top level is an upstream error record (D17 when a hold is open;
forwarded otherwise, as today).

**OpenAI non-stream body.** The same rules applied to `choices[].message`.

**Anthropic.** Dispatch on `data.type`; a present `event:` name that differs is malformed.
These types are known: `message_start`, `message_delta`, `message_stop`, `ping`, `error`,
`content_block_start`, `content_block_delta`, `content_block_stop`. Any other type is
malformed. Block types:

- `text`, `thinking`, `redacted_thinking`: tool-free content.
- `server_tool_use`, `*_tool_result`, `mcp_tool_use`: tool-free, reported `unenforceable`.
- `tool_use`: tool-bearing.
- any other block type: tool-bearing, kind `Other` (fail closed).

### 4.3 Canonical assembly (any deviation → stream-level `on_failure`, code `Malformed`)

OpenAI, per choice:

- tool-call `index` values first appear in order 0, 1, 2, …; interleaving after that is fine;
- `id`, `type` and `function.name` (or `custom.name`) each appear in exactly one fragment;
- `type` never changes, and `function` and `custom` never appear in the same entry;
- `function.arguments` and `custom.input` are strings or `null` in every fragment (`null` adds
  nothing, as in every SDK);
- at the call's completion, `function.arguments` (Function and legacy calls) is `""` or one
  complete JSON value (§ 11, `incomplete_arguments`); `custom.input` is free text;
- a legacy `function_call` and `tool_calls` never appear in the same choice;
- no fragment arrives for a call after its choice's `finish_reason`.

Anthropic:

- a block's `index` equals the number of earlier `content_block_start` events;
- `tool_use.input` at `content_block_start` is `{}`;
- `message_start.message.content` is `[]`;
- no delta arrives for an unknown or stopped index;
- `partial_json` is a string.

### 4.4 Rewrite

Only frames that contain a blocked call are re-serialized.

**OpenAI streaming.** In every queued frame of a blocked call's choice:

- Remove the blocked entries from `delta.tool_calls`. Renumber the remaining entries'
  `index` from 0, in first-appearance order. Drop the key when it becomes empty.
- Remove `delta.function_call` when the legacy call is blocked.
- Keep `role`. Strip `logprobs`.
- Never drop a frame or a choice entry (§ 11, P-10): a choice entry whose blocked data is
  removed stays, with its `index` and an emptied `delta`.

Insert the notice as one chunk, `{"delta":{"content":"<notice>"}}` for that choice, right
before the frame that carries the choice's `finish_reason`. Copy `id`, `created`, `model` and
`system_fingerprint` from that frame when they are strings or numbers, and set `object` to
`chat.completion.chunk`. A notice owed at the end of the stream copies them from the last
accepted record. When text already streamed for the choice,
the notice starts with `\n\n`. `finish_reason` `"tool_calls"` or `"function_call"` becomes
`"stop"` when no call of the choice remains. Per-choice state survives the decision, so a
`finish_reason` that arrives after an `on_failure` close is rewritten too.

**OpenAI non-stream.** The same per-choice rules applied to `message`. The notice is appended
to `message.content` when it is a string, or set when it is `null`. When `content` is an
array, the notice is appended as a text part.

**Anthropic.** A blocked `tool_use` block becomes a `text` block at the same index:
`content_block_start {type:text, text:""}`, one `text_delta` with the notice, and
`content_block_stop`, each with its `event:` line. Its `input_json_delta` frames are dropped.
`message_delta.stop_reason` `"tool_use"` becomes `"end_turn"` when no `tool_use` block remains.
This applies wherever that frame arrives.

### 4.5 Notice and names

The notice reads `[paigasus] tool call "<name>" was blocked (<code>).`. `<code>` is the
kebab-case `BlockCode`. `<name>` is truncated to 128 bytes, and any byte outside
`[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]` becomes `_`.

### 4.6 Decision report schema

```json
{"v":1,"choice":0,"position":1,"name":"<sanitized>","name_sha256_8":"<8 hex>",
 "decision":"allow|block|unenforceable","basis":"decider|on_failure","code":"<kebab or null>"}
```

`name_sha256_8` disambiguates names that sanitize alike.

## 5. Components and data flow

### 5.1 `paigasus-gateway-core` (sans-IO)

```rust
pub struct Interceptor { /* per-stream state */ }
impl Interceptor {
    pub fn new(format: Format, limits: Limits, now: Instant) -> Self;
    pub fn push(&mut self, chunk: &[u8], now: Instant) -> Vec<Action>;
    pub fn decided(&mut self, hold: HoldId, r: Result<Vec<Decision>, DeciderError>, now: Instant) -> Vec<Action>;
    pub fn tick(&mut self, now: Instant) -> Vec<Action>;
    pub fn finish(&mut self, now: Instant) -> Vec<Action>;   // clean upstream end
    pub fn abort(&mut self) -> Vec<Action>;                  // upstream error, D17
}
pub enum Action { Emit(Bytes), Decide { hold: HoldId, calls: Vec<ToolCall> }, Wake(Instant), Count(Metric) }
pub fn intercept_body(format: Format, body: &[u8]) -> Result<BodyPlan, Malformed>;  // non-stream
```

The terminal error frame is a constructor argument, so the Anthropic path can pass its own.
Modules: `sse`, `json` (strict parse, D5; skeletons use `Cow<str>` / `&RawValue`, never
`&str`, because arguments always contain escapes), `openai`, `anthropic`, `turn`, `assembly`,
`rewrite`, `report`, `types`. Dependencies: `serde`, `serde_json` (`raw_value`), `bytes`,
`thiserror`, `sha2`. No tokio, futures, axum or reqwest.

### 5.2 Gateway wiring

- `config.rs`: `ToolInterceptionConfig { enabled, max_record_bytes (1 MiB), max_held_bytes
  (4 MiB), max_hold_secs (300), decide_timeout_secs (5), keepalive_secs (10), on_failure }`.
  Validation: all non-zero, `max_record_bytes <= max_held_bytes`, `keepalive_secs <
  max_hold_secs`.
- `chat.rs`, streaming: the relay's upstream reader feeds raw bytes to `UsageScanner` first,
  then to `Interceptor::push`. On `Err` it calls `abort()`, emits the actions, and then emits
  `TERMINAL_SSE_ERROR` (owned by the interceptor when enabled). The relay state owns at most
  one pending decider future and one `tokio::time::Sleep`. It polls them with the upstream
  in `select!` (biased: decider, timer, upstream).
- `chat.rs`, non-stream: `non_stream_usage` reads the original body. Then `intercept_body`
  runs: allow-all returns the original bytes; a block re-serializes once. For a 2xx body that
  is malformed, `block` returns 502 `tool-interception-malformed-response` (the charge is
  settled as for the forwarded body); `allow` forwards it. Bodies over `max_held_bytes` are
  malformed.
- `AppState` gets `Arc<dyn ToolCallDecider>`, which is `AllowAll` for now.
  `DecisionContext` is built in the handler from `CallerContext` and the request ids.
- Metrics, in `paigasus-observability/src/names.rs` plus `ALL`:
  - `gateway_tool_interception_records_dropped_total{reason}`: `malformed`, `after_done`,
    `late_fragment`, `oversized`;
  - `gateway_tool_interception_decisions_total{decision,basis}`;
  - `gateway_tool_interception_on_failure_total{code}`;
  - `gateway_tool_interception_hold_seconds` (histogram).

### 5.3 Observe mode (`on_failure = "allow"`)

On overflow or hold timeout, the affected holds are released as they are. Later fragments of
those calls are forwarded unheld. When such a call completes, the decider is still consulted
(unless it outgrew `max_held_bytes`, § 11),
and the decision is reported with `basis: "on_failure"` and is not enforced. On a malformed
record while the queue is non-empty, or a canonical-form deviation, the stream switches to
pass-through: the rest is forwarded as received, and the switch
is reported once. A decider error or timeout means allow, with `basis: "on_failure"`.

## 6. Error handling

| Case | `block` | `allow` |
|---|---|---|
| Malformed record while the queue is non-empty, or a canonical-form deviation | Every open and later hold is blocked (`Malformed`). Later tool-bearing frames are dropped. | Pass-through (§ 5.3). |
| Record over `max_record_bytes` | As malformed. | As malformed. |
| Queue over `max_held_bytes` | Open holds blocked (`HoldLimit`); their later fragments dropped. | § 5.3 |
| Hold over `max_hold_secs` | That hold blocked (`HoldLimit`). | § 5.3 |
| Decider error, timeout, wrong length | That hold blocked (`DeciderError`). | Allow, `basis: "on_failure"`. |
| Truncated hold (D10/D11) | Blocked (`Truncated`), then the stream ends as received. | Released as is. |
| Upstream transport error / error record mid-hold | D17. | D17. |
| Non-2xx upstream | Forwarded as today, no interception. | Same. |

## 7. Repo gates the new crate touches

- `rs/Cargo.toml` `members`: one literal line (SMA-663 A11).
- `ci/affected-graph/run.sh`: the `lockfile->all-lint` set, plus a new
  `gateway-core->consumer-tasks` case (a gateway-core source edit selects the gateway's
  build, test and lint, and `gateway-console-ts:test-e2e`).
- The crate's `moon.yml`: `fileGroups.upstreams`, `dependsOn` as for the other lib crates. The
  gateway's `moon.yml` gains the dependency.
- Error code: `ERROR_REASON_TOOL_INTERCEPTION_MALFORMED_RESPONSE = 313` in
  `contracts/proto/paigasus/common/v1/error.proto` (gateway range). This also needs:
  - codegen drift for rs, py and ts;
  - a `GatewayError` variant;
  - the `ci/error-registry/check.py` MANIFEST row and its membership test;
  - the `mapError` mapping in `ts/packages/paigasus-sdk/src/chat.ts`.
- Metric names: `paigasus-observability` `names.rs` and `ALL` (observability drift).
- `sha2` is already in `rs/Cargo.lock`; the plan picks the existing version so `:deny` and

## 8. Testing

### 8.1 Differential oracle (the security proof)

`tests/oracle/` holds Rust models of these client accumulators:

- openai-python `accumulate_delta` / `ChatCompletionStreamState`;
- openai-node `ChatCompletionStream`;
- LangChain's chunk merge;
- anthropic-python `MessageStream`;
- this repo's `chat-stream.ts` and `paigasus-sdk/src/chat.ts` parsers.

Each model takes the emitted bytes and returns the tool calls that client would run. The

**Property P1 (I1).** For every generated upstream stream and every model M, every call M

**Generators** are grammar-based. They produce conforming streams and every shape named in

## 11. Implementation rulings (2026-11-11)

The controller made these rulings during implementation. Each one changes or settles
behaviour that §§ 3–6 left open, and each fails closed. The sentences they made stale are
edited in place above (D12's reason, § 4.3, § 4.4, § 5.2).

**OpenAI classification and canonical form.**

- **`choice_order` (P-10 (a)).** A choice index seen for the first time must equal the number
  of choices seen so far, or the record is `Deviation("choice_order")`. openai-python finds a
  stream choice by list position, so choice 1 before choice 0 would merge two choices' calls.
- **Choice-0-only tool data.** A tool-call fragment (`tool_calls` or `function_call`) in a
  choice whose `index` is not 0 is `Deviation("multi_choice_tool_calls")`. Tool data in a
  choice entry at array position other than 0 of its chunk is `Deviation("choice_position")`.
  LangChain reads `choices[0]` of each chunk and ignores `choice.index`. **Limitation:** an
  `n > 1` request whose later choices call tools is not supported while interception is on. It
  gets `on_failure` (block, or pass-through in observe mode). The non-stream body applies the
  same rules, as `Malformed`.
- **Duplicate choice index.** A chunk that names one choice index twice is
  `Malformed("duplicate_choice_index")`.
- **The `object` rule.** Stream: a chunk that carries tool data or a `finish_reason` must have
  `object` exactly `"chat.completion.chunk"`, or it is `Malformed("object")`; openai-python
  skips any other chunk. Body: `object` must be `"chat.completion"` only when the body carries
  tool calls.
- **`type_shape_mismatch`.** A `type` that disagrees with the entry's body shape (`function` or
  `custom`) is a deviation, never kind `Other`: clients ignore `type` and run the body. Kind
  `Other` applies only when no `function` or `custom` body arrived.
- **`incomplete_arguments`.** At completion, OpenAI function and legacy-function arguments
  (stream and body) must be `""` or one complete JSON value; Anthropic `tool_use` input at
  `content_block_stop` the same. Otherwise the call is `Deviation("incomplete_arguments")`
  (`Malformed` in a body). `""` is presented to the decider as `"{}"`. Custom-tool input is
  free text and is not checked. Reason: LangChain and anthropic-python partial-parse truncated
  JSON, so the decider would see different arguments than the client runs.
- **`long_identifier`.** A tool-call id or name over 1024 bytes is `Deviation("long_identifier")`
  (`Malformed` in a body), in both protocols: OpenAI at the phase-1 check, Anthropic at
  `content_block_start` for `tool_use`, server and other blocks. Real ids and names are under
  100 bytes. A completed block keeps its name for the stream's life, so up to 4096 blocks of
  near-record-cap names would be retained outside held-byte accounting. A completed Anthropic
  block also moves its id out instead of cloning it.
- **`second_finish`.** A second `finish_reason` for one choice is a deviation, for tool-free
  choices too.
- **Arguments may be `null`** in a fragment (§ 4.3). It adds nothing, as in every SDK.
- **P-10 (b), never drop.** The rewrite never removes a choice entry and never drops a frame
  (§ 4.4), so the gateway's own rewrite cannot shift openai-python's positions.
- **Notice meta.** A notice chunk copies `id`, `created`, `model` and `system_fingerprint` only
  when they are strings or numbers, and always says `"object":"chat.completion.chunk"`. Only
  accepted records update the meta that the closing notice uses, so a dropped record cannot
  name it.
- **Prior OpenAI calls.** A request's prior assistant `tool_calls` entry reads `function.name`
  and `function.arguments`, or `custom.name` and `custom.input`. An entry with neither body,
  with both, or with a body that disagrees with its `type` makes the turn
  `Unavailable("malformed")`, as a `function` without a `name` does (D19).

**Anthropic.**

- **`block_interleave`.** A `content_block_start` while an earlier block is still open is a
  deviation. LangChain routes `input_json_delta` to the most recent start, not to
  `event.index`.
- **Synthesized stop frame.** A blocked block's `content_block_stop` is re-emitted as the
  synthesized `{"type":"content_block_stop","index":i}`, never the upstream payload.

**Bodies and numbers.**

- **`lossy_number`.** A body (either format) holding a number outside `u64`/`i64` that is an
  integral `f64` with magnitude of 2^53 or more is `Malformed("lossy_number")`. serde_json would
  round it, and the decider would see a different number than the client. The rule applies to
  stream kind-Other calls too, in both protocols: their arguments are the parsed raw entries, so
  a raw entry holding such a number makes the call's completion `Deviation("lossy_number")`.
- **`preserve_order`.** `paigasus-gateway-core` enables serde_json's `preserve_order`, so a
  re-serialized frame or body keeps the upstream key order in every build.

**Strict JSON scope (I-1).** The D5 envelope rules (case-folded classifier keys, `constructor`,
`prototype`) apply to envelope keys only. Tool argument and schema data gets JSON validity,
duplicate-key rejection at every depth, non-finite rejection and `__proto__` rejection, but not
the case-fold or `constructor`/`prototype` checks: the classifiers never read inside it, and a
tool may take an argument named `Id` or `constructor`. That data is OpenAI function and legacy
arguments, Anthropic `tool_use` and `server_tool_use` `input`, a request's
`tools[].function.parameters` and `functions[].parameters`, an Anthropic request's
`tools[].input_schema`, and prior-call inputs in the request. In a whole-record, body or
request parse, the value of an `input`, `parameters` or `input_schema` key gets these rules.

**Interceptor and limits.**

- **Wrong-length decision vectors.** A decision vector whose length differs from the calls'
  blocks every call of the hold with `DeciderError` (stream and body), not only the missing ones.
- **`after_done` before `oversized`.** After `[DONE]` (or `message_stop`) every record is
  dropped and counted as `after_done`, an oversized one included. It never becomes a stream
  failure.
- **Oversized records** are always dropped and counted with the new `records_dropped` reason
  `oversized` (§ 5.2), in both `on_failure` modes (P-3). With `allow` the stream then switches
  to pass-through.
- **Observed holds are bounded (D13).** A hold under observe mode (§ 5.3) keeps assembling for
  the report, but once it retains more than `max_held_bytes` of arguments and raw entries it
  drops them and is never decided: no decision and no report entry, as for a pass-through
  call. Its frames still flow. A completed hold keeps no arguments in either protocol.
- **86 400 s caps.** Every `[tool_interception]` `*_secs` value is capped at 86 400 by
  validation; `Instant + Duration` would otherwise panic on overflow.

3	Linear: SMA-757 (parent SMA-747). Related: SMA-749 (the oracle and the interceptor), SMA-752
4	(argument-reading policies). This change must land before SMA-752 or as part of it.

6	## 1. Intent
7	
8	The differential oracle of SMA-749 (`rs/crates/libs/paigasus-gateway-core/tests/support/oracle.rs`)
9	checks invariant I1: every call that a client model derives from the gateway's output was decided

16	That tolerance is sound only while deciders read the tool name alone. SMA-752 adds policies that
17	read arguments. A prefix of allowed arguments can then be a call that the policy denies. An
18	example: a policy allows `read_file` only for a `path` under `/workspace/`. The decider sees

103	  were never next to a function call.
104	- R5. Not measured: a `custom` call and a function call in one response. In 10 tries the models
105	  never did it, even when the prompt asked for both.
106	- Every chunk has an `obfuscation` string field, which pads the chunks to a uniform length. So
107	  repeated runs often have the same byte size. The completion and call ids differ in every run.
108	
109	Not covered: Azure OpenAI (for example its content-filter chunks), and self-hosted upstreams
110	(SMA-749 T2).
111	
112	One recording for each model and scenario (12 files, 88 KiB) is kept as a fixture next to the
113	script.
114	
115	## 3. Decisions
116	
117	| Id | Decision |
118	|----|----------|
119	| D1 | Scope: the oracle **and** the interceptor (Sven, 2026-11-14). An oracle-only change cannot pass honestly (§ 2). |
120	| D2 | Oracle rule: **reject every strict partial.** At an excused raise, a call in the client's snapshot must match an allowed call exactly (the non-partial rules, including `""` against `{}`). A re-decide of the prefix was the first draft. It was dropped: it proves I1 only for the test deciders, and the gateway never asks the production decider about a prefix. This rule is decider-free, and it is what I1 says. Changed after the review. Confirmed by Sven at Gate 1 (2026-11-14). |
121	| D3 | Interceptor rule: each record shape in § 5 becomes a canonical-form deviation (a stream-level `on_failure`, as every § 4.3 deviation of SMA-749 is), or a malformed record. The rules name shapes, not one SDK. |
122	| D4 | Anthropic: no interceptor change (§ 2.3). The anthropic-python model's partial parser is fixed to match jiter (§ 6.3). Bodies: no change (a body has no fragments). So a body tool call reads `"type": null` as absent, as before; § 5.3 applies to streams only. One exception: § 5.8 applies to a body `function_call` too, because the stream and the body share one parser for it and real OpenAI sends no such key in either. |
123	| D5 | The generators render every shape of § 2.2, so P1 covers each one with random cuts and deciders (§ 7.1). |
124	| D6 | H1 and H2 are fixed in this change, not in a later sweep. Confirmed by Sven at Gate 1 (2026-11-14). |
125	| D7 | Real OpenAI streams are recorded and kept as fixtures (§ 2.4), at Sven's request. Every recording must pass with no deviation (§ 7.3). |
126	
127	## 4. The oracle change
128	
129	In `arguments_match`, the `partial` flag no longer allows a prefix. A snapshot at an excused raise
130	is checked with the same rules as a complete run. The raise only excuses the fact that the client
131	raised, and that it may hold fewer calls. Concretely:
132	
133	- `json_prefix` is deleted.
134	- The `partial` branch of `arguments_match` (`starts_with`, and `json_prefix` for parsed values) is
135	  deleted, so `arguments_match` loses the `partial` parameter.
136	- `check_i1` keeps the `partial` state only to excuse the raise. The doc comments of `check_i1`,
137	  `arguments_match` and the module header must say that a partial call is never accepted, and why
138	  (SMA-752).
139	- Matching stays first-fit over candidates, and it is exact. Two allowed calls with the same choice,
140	  kind and name but other arguments cannot be confused, because only an exact match is accepted.
141	
142	Kind `other` keeps its current rule: arguments are not compared, because the decided form is the
143	raw entry. This is a known limit for SMA-752 policies that read the arguments of a kind Other call
144	(§ 9).
145	
146	## 5. The interceptor changes (OpenAI stream)
147	
148	"Open call" means a call of choice 0 whose first fragment has arrived, before the choice's
149	`finish_reason`. All checks run on the copy before anything is changed, as every canonical check
150	does, so a deviation leaves no half-applied state.
151	
152	### 5.1 `fragment_after_bodyless_entry` (P-M3)
153	
154	A tool-call entry is **bodyless** when it has no `function` object (`Fragment.function` is `None`):
155	a `custom` entry, an entry with only `index`, `id` or `type`, or `"function": null`. LangChain
156	raises at the first record that holds a bodyless entry in its choice, and it drops that whole
157	record. So, once a record holds a bodyless entry, that record and every later record must hold no
158	fragment for a call that existed **before that record was applied**. Such a fragment is
159	`Deviation("fragment_after_bodyless_entry")`.
160	
161	- A call that starts in the bodyless record or later is never seen by LangChain. LangChain then
162	  runs fewer calls, which is fail-closed.
163	- The boundary is renewed at every bodyless record, not only at the first one, because the
164	  rewrite can remove an earlier blocked bodyless call. Then a later bodyless record is the first
165	  one in the output. Example: record 1 holds custom call 0 `blocked_early`, record 2 starts
166	  function call 1, record 3 holds custom call 2, and record 4 continues call 1. When call 0 is
167	  blocked, LangChain raises at record 3 with a prefix of call 1. So record 4 is the deviation.
168	- `Check` stores the number of calls that existed before the latest bodyless record was applied
169	  (`Option<usize>`, `None` until then). The value only grows.
170	- A bodyless fragment that continues a custom or Other call does not renew the boundary and is
171	  not a deviation. The first record of that call was bodyless already: it stays in the output
172	  before this record when the call is allowed, and the rewrite removes both when it is blocked.
173	  So a custom call that streams in contiguous records after a function call stays conforming.
174	- The rule is slightly too broad, on purpose: a later fragment that adds nothing
175	  (`"arguments":""`, `null`, `"function":{}`) is also a deviation. Exempting it adds a case for no
176	  practical gain.
177	
178	### 5.2 `choice_without_delta` and `chunk_without_choices` (P-a, P-b, P-f)
179	
180	While choice 0 has an open call, **and in the record that opens a call of choice 0** (the record
181	carries tool data for choice 0):
182	
183	- a chunk with no `choices` key is `Deviation("chunk_without_choices")`;
184	- a choice entry with no `delta` key, in any position, is `Deviation("choice_without_delta")`.
185	  One exception: the entry of choice 0 that carries its `finish_reason` may omit `delta`. No
186	  fragment can follow it (`late_fragment`), so every call is complete when a client raises there.
187	
188	`"delta": null` stays `Malformed("delta")` in every position (SMA-749 classifier); inside an open
189	call the queue is non-empty, so it is already a stream-level failure.
190	
191	Outside an open call these records stay as they are today (classified as tool-free). This limits
192	the rule to the place where a raise can cut a call.
193	
194	The record that opens a call counts (P-f): a raise later in that record cuts the call after its
195	first fragment. One predicate in `stream.rs` (`in_call`: an open call, or this record carries tool
196	data for choice 0) decides this for § 5.2 and § 5.7, so the two rules cannot drift.
197	
198	### 5.3 A present `type` key counts as the type fragment (P-c)
199	
200	`"type": null` is read as "absent" today (`opt_str`, `json.rs`), so a later `"type": null` passes
201	`repeated_type`. In a tool-call fragment, a present `type` key, `null` included, counts as the type
202	fragment. A second one is `repeated_type`. A first `"type": null` with a `function` body is
203	`type_shape_mismatch` at completion. The builder must check that the existing `type`-absent
204	streams in the fixtures and generators stay conforming.
205	
206	### 5.4 H1: a top-level `chunk` key
207	
208	A chunk that has a top-level `chunk` key is `Malformed("chunk_key")` (the record is dropped, with
209	the same § 6 behaviour of SMA-749 as other malformed records). No real OpenAI-compatible upstream
210	sends it. The key is added to the classifier key list in `json.rs`, so case-folded forms are
211	rejected the same way as other classifier keys.
212	
213	### 5.5 H2: a top-level `type` of `content.delta`
214	
215	A chunk whose top-level `type` is the string `content.delta` and that carries tool data
216	(`tool_calls`, `function_call`) or a `finish_reason` is `Malformed("content_delta_type")`.
217	LangChain skips such a record, so the decider and LangChain would see different calls.
218	
219	### 5.6 Common consequences
220	
221	- Real OpenAI did not send any of these shapes in 60 recorded streams (§ 2.4, R1 and R2). So no
222	  rule fires on that traffic. The recorded fixtures pin this (§ 7.3). A self-hosted or Azure
223	  upstream that sends one of these shapes gets `on_failure`. The upstream bytes already make at
224	  least one supported client raise or misread in every case.
225	- **`"type": null` on every continuation fragment.** An upstream that sends `"type": null` on
226	  each later fragment of a call (for example a server that dumps pydantic models without
227	  `exclude_none`) now gets `repeated_type`, so `on_failure` runs on every tool stream from it. The
228	  rule is necessary: openai-python replaces `type` on such a fragment and its
229	  `new_tool.type == "function"` assert raises (§ 5.3, P-c). How common this upstream shape is was
230	  not measured. Real OpenAI does not send it (§ 2.4, R2).
231	- **Observe mode trade-off.** Under `on_failure = allow`, the deviating record is not emitted and
232	  later records are forwarded unclassified (SMA-749 § 5.3). A stream that was enforced before (for
233	  example an interleaved function and custom call) now reaches openai-python and openai-node in
234	  pass-through, without the deviating record. For P-M3 that record holds the `custom` entry and any
235	  fragments in it. Observe mode is not a security mode, and every SMA-749 deviation behaves this
236	  way. This spec does not change that behaviour.
237	- Each deviation is reported as `RecordDropped("malformed")` and `OnFailure("malformed")`, as the
238	  existing deviations are. An operator cannot tell the new deviations apart. This is unchanged.
239	- The rules and their reasons go into the module docs: `src/openai/assembly.rs` for § 5.1 and
240	  § 5.3, `src/openai/stream.rs` for § 5.2 and § 5.7, and `src/openai/classify.rs` for § 5.4,
241	  § 5.5 and § 5.8. The SMA-749 spec is not edited; this spec
242	  supersedes its § 4.3 list for these shapes.
243	
244	### 5.7 `array_outside_tool_calls` (P-e)
245	
246	Inside a call of choice 0 (the `in_call` predicate of § 5.2), a delta that holds an array outside
247	the `tool_calls` array itself is `Deviation("array_outside_tool_calls")`. The array can be the
248	value of any delta key other than `tool_calls`, or of any key of a tool-call entry, its `function`
249	and `custom` objects included, or of any key of a legacy `function_call`. It counts at any depth
250	below those keys. The rule applies to the choice entries in every position of the record, as
251	§ 5.2 does: a raise in any choice stops openai-python for the whole stream.
252	
253	- openai-python's `accumulate_delta` merges a list by `index` when the earlier list holds
254	  non-scalar entries. A later list whose entry is not a dict raises `TypeError`, so the client
255	  keeps a strict prefix of the call. The rule names the shape (an array where no real upstream
256	  sends one), not the exact raise condition.
257	- The rule also covers an array nested in an object (`{"foo":{"bar":[…]}}`), because
258	  `accumulate_delta` merges dicts recursively. The review named only the first level. A kind
259	  Other entry with an array in its raw body is a deviation too: that is fail-closed.
260	- Choice-level keys (for example `logprobs`) are not merged as a delta. They are not checked.
261	- The recorded streams (§ 2.4) and the conforming fixtures hold no array outside `tool_calls`.
262	  The recorded delta keys are `content`, `function_call`, `refusal`, `role` and `tool_calls`.
263	- Outside a call the shape stays conforming: a raise there cuts no call.
264	
265	### 5.8 `function_call_key` (P-d)
266	
267	A legacy `function_call` object with a key other than `name` and `arguments` is
268	`Malformed("function_call_key")`. This applies in every stream record and in a non-stream body:
269	`classify::legacy_call` reads the object for both.
270	
271	- LangChain merges the extra key into `additional_kwargs["function_call"]`. When a later fragment
272	  gives it another JSON type, `merge_dicts` raises `TypeError`. Its snapshot then holds the
273	  arguments merged so far, which is a strict prefix when more arguments follow.
274	- The rule is malformed, not a deviation, and it does not depend on an open call: no real OpenAI
275	  stream or body sends another key (§ 2.4: the recorded `function_call` keys are `name` and
276	  `arguments`). A body with such a key is `Malformed`, which changes the body path (D4).
277	- In a stream, the record is dropped. Inside an open hold this is a stream-level failure, as for
278	  every malformed record (SMA-749 § 6).
279	
280	## 6. Model changes in the oracle
281	
282	### 6.1 None for the raise paths
283	
284	The OpenAI models already raise as the real SDKs do on P-a, P-b, P-c and P-M3 (cited sources in
285	`oracle.rs`). They are not changed.
286	
287	### 6.2 LangChain H1 and H2
288	
289	The LangChain model already reads `chunk.choices` and skips `content.delta` records. It is not
290	changed.
291	
292	### 6.3 anthropic-python partial parse
293	
294	`Partial::value` in `oracle.rs` must drop an unfinished number or literal at the end of the input,
295	with its key, and not raise, as jiter does (§ 2.3). The doc comment must cite the jiter version
296	measured. A unit test pins the three measured inputs: `{"n":10.` gives `{}`, `{"n":1e` gives `{}`,
297	`{"a":"x","n":10.` gives `{"a":"x"}`.
298	
299	## 7. Tests
300	
301	### 7.1 Generator quirks
302	
303	`tests/support/streams.rs` gets one OpenAI `Quirk` for each shape of § 2.2 and § 5: a bodyless
304	entry interleaved inside an open call (it exists), a chunk without `choices`, a choice entry
305	without `delta`, a `"type": null` fragment, a top-level `chunk` key with a tool call, a
306	`content.delta` record with a fragment, two records with an array outside `tool_calls`
307	(§ 5.7), and two legacy fragments with an extra key that changes type (§ 5.8). The quirk for a choice entry without `delta` also adds `{"index":1}` behind the
308	record that opens a call (P-f). Each quirk must be able to land between two fragments of
309	an allowed call. The generators must also emit an Anthropic input with a decimal number, split
310	inside the number.
311	
312	### 7.2 A property test of the oracle (the issue's "fails on the current tolerance")
313	
314	A new proptest drives `check_i1` directly, with no interceptor, on a generated OpenAI stream. It has
315	an allowed function call 0 whose arguments are split into two fragments, and a raise record from
316	§ 2.2 (P-M3, P-a, P-b or P-c, chosen by the strategy) between them. `decided` holds the calls, all
317	`Allow`. The output is the upstream bytes, so the raise is excused and the partial path runs. The
318	test asserts that `check_i1` returns `Err`, and that the message names the model and call 0.
319	
320	- On the current oracle it fails: the prefix is accepted.
321	- After § 4 it passes.
322	
323	A second case puts the raise record after the last fragment of call 0. The test asserts `Ok`, so
324	the oracle does not simply reject every excused raise.
325	
326	`ToolCall` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the test builds the decided calls from `parse_body`
327	(`BodyCalls.calls`) and changes fields on a clone, or with a test-support constructor if one is
328	needed. This test lives in one test file (for example `tests/oracle.rs`), not in `support/`,
329	because `support/` is compiled into every test binary.
330	
331	### 7.3 Fixtures
332	
333	One fixture per new rule under `tests/fixtures/openai/malformed/`, generated by
334	`tests/fixtures/make_fixtures.py`, each with a row in `malformed_shapes_follow_section_6`:
335	`fragment_after_bodyless_entry`, `chunk_without_choices`, `choice_without_delta`, `type_null`,
336	`chunk_key`, `content_delta_type`, `array_outside_tool_calls` (§ 5.7),
337	`choice_without_delta_in_opening_record` (§ 5.2, P-f), `function_call_key` (§ 5.8) and
338	`fragment_after_blocked_bodyless_entry` (§ 5.1, a renewed boundary). The
339	conforming fixture `bodyless_type_null` pins a bare `{"index":0,"type":null}` call: kind Other,
340	named `unknown` by the core and by the oracle.
341	
342	Each fixture has an **allowed** call (`read_file` with `{"v":"abcdefgh"}`, a function call or a
343	legacy call for § 5.8) whose fragments are split around the rule's record. The canary is **in
344	the deviating record itself** (for example a `"note":"CANARY-…"` key), not in a separate
345	`blocked_*` call: a separate later call is forwarded in observe mode after the deviation, so its
346	canary would leak there. Then `every_fixture_holds_i1_for_every_client` reds for that fixture
347	under `allow-all` and `block-by-name` when its rule is removed (§ 7.4). Under `block-all` the
348	allowed call is blocked and rewritten out, so no partial call reaches a client and I1 cannot red. The H1 fixture puts a `blocked_*` call
349	inside `chunk`.
350	
351	The recorded streams of § 2.4 are kept in `openai/recorded`. They are **not** in the fixture sets
352	of `tests/fixtures.rs` (`SETS`), because the canary and row tests assume the hand-built names.
353	`recorded_streams_pass_unchanged` replays them with `on_failure = block`:
354	
355	- One push per file under each of the three deciders (`allow-all`, `block-all`,
356	  `block-by-name`): the stream ends, there is no `RecordDropped` or `OnFailure` metric, and I1
357	  holds (`check_i1`). Under `allow-all` the output is also payload-identical to the input, and
358	  every OpenAI model derives the decided calls from it (the same kinds and names, in order; I1
359	  compares the arguments).
360	- Every single split point of every file (one cut), under `allow-all`: the stream ends, the
361	  metrics are clean, and the output is byte-identical to the one-push output. So it is
362	  payload-identical to the input, and the client runs of the one-push pass hold for it. The
363	  files run in parallel threads (about 74 000 drives).
364	
365	So a future rule that rejects real OpenAI traffic reds at once. `capture.py` stays next to the
366	recordings, so they can be recorded again. It reads the API key from a file and never prints it.
367	It is not run in CI.
368	
369	### 7.4 Proof that each half bites
370	
371	The plan must record each of these as a measured red. Each mutation must compile (`-D warnings`
372	applies to test targets) and is reverted by deleting the marked edit, not by `git checkout`.
373	
374	1. The § 7.2 test, written first, against the current oracle. (Red 1 is the same state as
375	   mutation 3 below: the prefix branch exists. Measure it once, before § 4.)
376	2. `every_fixture_holds_i1_for_every_client` with § 4 and the § 7.3 fixtures, before § 5. Every
377	   new fixture must red, by name. This is deterministic, unlike a random P1 run.
378	3. After all changes: restore the prefix acceptance in `arguments_match`. The § 7.2 test must red.
379	4. After all changes: delete each § 5 rule in turn. Its fixture must red in
380	   `every_fixture_holds_i1_for_every_client`, not only in the `stream_failure` column.
381	5. After all changes: restore the raising `Partial` behaviour. The § 6.3 unit test must red.
382	
383	`openai_p1_and_p2_hold` and `anthropic_p1_and_p2_hold` must pass at 10 000 cases after all
384	changes. A random red in them before § 5 is expected but is not part of the proof.
385	
386	## 8. Changes to the test deciders
387	
388	None are needed for the proof: D2 is decider-free. The existing three deciders stay.
389	
390	## 9. Non-goals
391	
392	- `json.rs` `DATA_KEYS` matches `input`, `input_schema` and `parameters` by key name only. That is
393	  safe while no classifier reads below those keys. SMA-750 or SMA-752 must re-check it when one
394	  does. This change does not touch it.
395	- Kind `other` arguments are not compared (§ 4). An SMA-752 policy that reads them needs its own
396	  rule.
397	- A BOM-prefixed first record that openai-python ignores on the upstream bytes reaches it after the
398	  SMA-749 D2 BOM strip. With a chunk that has no `choices`, the client then raises. This is
399	  availability only: no tool call is affected (a hidden first record with a call makes the client
400	  run fewer calls). It is SMA-749 behaviour, and this change does not fix it. The generator keeps
401	  such records off the first line when it emits a BOM.
402	- No change to the Anthropic assembly, to bodies (except § 5.8), or to the decider port
403	  (`ToolCallDecider`).
404	- The OpenAI Responses API (`/v1/responses`) is SMA-769, which starts after this change. It needs
405	  its own ingress, format and oracle models. It takes the D2 rule and the recording method of this
406	  spec from the start (§ 2.4).
407	- Support for an upstream that sends `"type": null` on every continuation fragment (§ 5.6). It
408	  gets `on_failure`; this change does not measure or relax that.
409	- The LangChain model is `<not pinned: modelled only>` (`oracle.rs`). This change does not pin it.
410	  If the real SDK does not raise where the model raises, the § 5 rules still hold: they only reject
411	  streams.
412	
413	## 10. Left to the builder
414	
415	- The exact doc-comment text, the proptest strategies, and the fixture contents within § 7.3.
416	- Whether a test-support constructor for `ToolCall` is needed (§ 7.2).
417	- The exact place of each § 5 check in `Check::apply` or the classifier, within the rule that
418	  every check runs on the copy before anything changes.
