# SMA-757: no partial calls at a client raise, in the oracle and in the interceptor

Linear: SMA-757 (parent SMA-747). Related: SMA-749 (the oracle and the interceptor), SMA-752
(argument-reading policies). This change must land before SMA-752 or as part of it.

## 1. Intent

The differential oracle of SMA-749 (`rs/crates/libs/paigasus-gateway-core/tests/support/oracle.rs`)
checks invariant I1: every call that a client model derives from the gateway's output was decided
`Allow`, with the same choice, kind, name and arguments that the decider saw (SMA-749 spec § 2).
When a client model raises partway through a stream, and the raise is excused (`core_failed`, or
the client also raises on the upstream bytes), the oracle accepts a call whose arguments are only a
**prefix** of the decided arguments (`json_prefix` for parsed values, `starts_with` for raw
strings).

That tolerance is sound only while deciders read the tool name alone. SMA-752 adds policies that
read arguments. A prefix of allowed arguments can then be a call that the policy denies. An
example: a policy allows `read_file` only for a `path` under `/workspace/`. The decider sees
`{"path":"/workspace/a"}` and allows it. A client that holds the prefix `{"path":"/wor"}` holds a
call that the policy would block. The oracle must catch this, and the gateway must not produce it.

## 2. Measured current state (2026-11-14, `origin/main` 2d58afd6)

### 2.1 The generated suite

The oracle was instrumented temporarily, and `tests/properties.rs` and `tests/fixtures.rs` were run
once (10 000 cases per format for P1).

- M1. The strict-prefix branch (a partial result that is a prefix but not equal) fired **9 times**.
  All 9 were the LangChain model, on OpenAI streams, through the parsed (`json_prefix`) branch.
  Examples: `{"v":"pihn"}` of `{"v":"pihnarwopuv"}`, `{}` of `{"v":"vgfpua"}`.
- M2. The raw `starts_with` branch and the anthropic-python model fired **0 times** in the
  generated suite. § 2.2 shows that this comes from the generators, not from the interceptor.
- M3. All 9 streams have one shape. The interceptor forwards the upstream records verbatim after
  the decision. A function call's argument fragments are interleaved with a later tool-call entry
  that has no `function` body (a `custom` call). LangChain reads `rtc["function"].get(...)` and
  raises `AttributeError` at that record. The upstream bytes raise the same way, so the raise is
  excused. `core_failed` was `false` in all 9.

### 2.2 Hand-built probes (one allowed call, `{"v":"ab` + one record + `cdefgh"}`, `allow-all`)

The adversarial review found more raise paths. Each probe was driven through the interceptor and
every OpenAI model. In each case `core_failed` was `false` and the upstream bytes raise too.

| Id | Record between the two fragments | Models that hold a strict prefix |
|----|----------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| P-M3 | a `custom` tool-call entry | LangChain (`{"v":"ab"}`) |
| P-a | a chunk with no `choices` key | openai-python, openai-node (raw `{"v":"ab`) |
| P-b | a choice entry with no `delta` key | openai-python (raw), LangChain (parsed) |
| P-c | a fragment `{"index":0,"type":null}` of the same call | openai-python (raw), LangChain (parsed) |
| P-e | two records: an unknown delta key with an indexed list, then a scalar list (`{"foo":[{"index":0}]}`, then `{"foo":[1]}`). The same under a tool-call entry key (`"x":[…]`) or a `function` key. | openai-python (raw `{"v":"ab`) |
| P-e′ | as P-e, but the indexed list is in a text record before the call, and the scalar list is in the record that opens the call | openai-python (raw `{"v":"ab`) |
| P-f | an earlier text record, then one record with the fragment that opens the call at position 0 and a choice entry `{"index":1}` with no `delta` at position 1 | openai-python (raw `{"v":"ab`) |
| P-d | a legacy `function_call` whose extra key changes JSON type | LangChain raises. It merges `arguments` before the extra key, so it holds the full call **only when the type change is in the last fragment**. When the change is in a middle fragment and more arguments follow, LangChain holds a strict prefix (raw `{"v":"abcd`, final review probe G2). |

P-d was first recorded with the type change in the last fragment only, so its first result
("none") was wrong for the general case. P-e, P-e′ and P-f were measured by the final branch review (2026-11-14, at 29784b6a), after the
rules of § 5.1 to § 5.5 were in place. openai-python raises in `accumulate_delta` (P-e) or at
`choice.delta` (P-f) and keeps what it merged before the raise. P-f was missed at first because
the "open call" state was read before the record that opens the call (§ 5.2).

Two related I1 holes have the same root cause (a record that the interceptor reads differently
from LangChain). They are not prefixes:

| Id | Record | Effect |
|----|--------|--------|
| H1 | `"choices":[]` and a top-level `chunk` object that holds `choices` with a tool call | LangChain reads `chunk.choices` when `choices` is empty. The interceptor does not read `chunk`. LangChain runs a call that **no decider saw**, under every decider. |
| H2 | a record with top-level `"type":"content.delta"` that carries an argument fragment | LangChain skips the record. The interceptor applies it. LangChain runs `{"v":"abcdefgh"}`, the decider saw `{"v":"abzzcdefgh"}`. |

### 2.3 Anthropic

The anthropic-python model raises on a buffer that ends inside a number (`{"n":10.`, `1e`, `-`).
Measured with jiter 0.19.0 (anthropic 2.3.0 requires `jiter<1,>=0.4.0`) in partial mode: jiter does
**not** raise. It drops the unfinished member (`{"n":10.` gives `{}`, `{"a":"x","n":10.` gives
`{"a":"x"}`). So there is no Anthropic gap, but the model is too strict. A false raise can make the
oracle excuse a snapshot that the real SDK never produces.

### 2.4 Real OpenAI streams (recorded 2026-11-14)

`tests/fixtures/openai/recorded/capture.py` recorded live Chat Completions streams with
`stream_options.include_usage`. It used three model families, five runs for each scenario, so
60 streams in total:

- `gpt-4.1`: parallel function calls and legacy `functions`. `custom` tools are rejected
  (`Invalid value: 'custom'`).
- `gpt-5.5`: parallel function calls, `custom` tools with function tools, a forced `custom` tool,
  and legacy `functions`.
- `gpt-6.1-terra`, with `reasoning_effort: "none"`: the same scenarios. On `/v1/chat/completions`,
  a `gpt-6` model accepts function tools only with `reasoning_effort: "none"`. Without it the API
  answers "Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported … use /v1/responses". The models
  `gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6-astra` do not accept `none`, so they cannot stream tool calls on Chat
  Completions at all. `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6-luna` accept `none`.

Results:

- R1. **No stream interleaves calls.** In all 60 streams, the fragments of each call are in
  contiguous records, and no other record is between two fragments of one call.
- R2. No stream holds a chunk without `choices`, a choice entry without `delta`, a
  `"type": null`, a top-level `chunk` or `type` key, or a choice other than 0.
- R3. The only chunk with empty `choices` is the final usage chunk (60 of 60).
- R4. A `custom` call streams as `{"index","id","type":"custom","custom":{…}}` and then
  `{"index","custom":{"input":…}}` entries. These are bodyless entries in the sense of § 5.1. They
  were never next to a function call.
- R5. Not measured: a `custom` call and a function call in one response. In 10 tries the models
  never did it, even when the prompt asked for both.
- Every chunk has an `obfuscation` string field, which pads the chunks to a uniform length. So
  repeated runs often have the same byte size. The completion and call ids differ in every run.

Not covered: Azure OpenAI (for example its content-filter chunks), and self-hosted upstreams
(SMA-749 T2).

One recording for each model and scenario (12 files, 88 KiB) is kept as a fixture next to the
script.

## 3. Decisions

| Id | Decision |
|----|----------|
| D1 | Scope: the oracle **and** the interceptor (Sven, 2026-11-14). An oracle-only change cannot pass honestly (§ 2). |
| D2 | Oracle rule: **reject every strict partial.** At an excused raise, a call in the client's snapshot must match an allowed call exactly (the non-partial rules, including `""` against `{}`). A re-decide of the prefix was the first draft. It was dropped: it proves I1 only for the test deciders, and the gateway never asks the production decider about a prefix. This rule is decider-free, and it is what I1 says. Changed after the review. Confirmed by Sven at Gate 1 (2026-11-14). |
| D3 | Interceptor rule: each record shape in § 5 becomes a canonical-form deviation (a stream-level `on_failure`, as every § 4.3 deviation of SMA-749 is), or a malformed record. The rules name shapes, not one SDK. |
| D4 | Anthropic: no interceptor change (§ 2.3). The anthropic-python model's partial parser is fixed to match jiter (§ 6.3). Bodies: no change (a body has no fragments). So a body tool call reads `"type": null` as absent, as before; § 5.3 applies to streams only. One exception: § 5.8 applies to a body `function_call` too, because the stream and the body share one parser for it and real OpenAI sends no such key in either. |
| D5 | The generators render every shape of § 2.2, so P1 covers each one with random cuts and deciders (§ 7.1). |
| D6 | H1 and H2 are fixed in this change, not in a later sweep. Confirmed by Sven at Gate 1 (2026-11-14). |
| D7 | Real OpenAI streams are recorded and kept as fixtures (§ 2.4), at Sven's request. Every recording must pass with no deviation (§ 7.3). |

## 4. The oracle change

In `arguments_match`, the `partial` flag no longer allows a prefix. A snapshot at an excused raise
is checked with the same rules as a complete run. The raise only excuses the fact that the client
raised, and that it may hold fewer calls. Concretely:

- `json_prefix` is deleted.
- The `partial` branch of `arguments_match` (`starts_with`, and `json_prefix` for parsed values) is
  deleted, so `arguments_match` loses the `partial` parameter.
- `check_i1` keeps the `partial` state only to excuse the raise. The doc comments of `check_i1`,
  `arguments_match` and the module header must say that a partial call is never accepted, and why
  (SMA-752).
- Matching stays first-fit over candidates, and it is exact. Two allowed calls with the same choice,
  kind and name but other arguments cannot be confused, because only an exact match is accepted.

Kind `other` keeps its current rule: arguments are not compared, because the decided form is the
raw entry. This is a known limit for SMA-752 policies that read the arguments of a kind Other call
(§ 9).

## 5. The interceptor changes (OpenAI stream)

"Open call" means a call of choice 0 whose first fragment has arrived, before the choice's
`finish_reason`. All checks run on the copy before anything is changed, as every canonical check
does, so a deviation leaves no half-applied state.

### 5.1 `fragment_after_bodyless_entry` (P-M3)

A tool-call entry is **bodyless** when it has no `function` object (`Fragment.function` is `None`):
a `custom` entry, an entry with only `index`, `id` or `type`, or `"function": null`. LangChain
raises at the first record that holds a bodyless entry in its choice, and it drops that whole
record. So, once a record holds a bodyless entry, that record and every later record must hold no
fragment for a call that existed **before that record was applied**. Such a fragment is
`Deviation("fragment_after_bodyless_entry")`.

- A call that starts in the bodyless record or later is never seen by LangChain. LangChain then
  runs fewer calls, which is fail-closed.
- The boundary is renewed at every bodyless record, not only at the first one, because the
  rewrite can remove an earlier blocked bodyless call. Then a later bodyless record is the first
  one in the output. Example: record 1 holds custom call 0 `blocked_early`, record 2 starts
  function call 1, record 3 holds custom call 2, and record 4 continues call 1. When call 0 is
  blocked, LangChain raises at record 3 with a prefix of call 1. So record 4 is the deviation.
- `Check` stores the number of calls that existed before the latest bodyless record was applied
  (`Option<usize>`, `None` until then). The value only grows.
- A bodyless fragment that continues a custom or Other call does not renew the boundary and is
  not a deviation. The first record of that call was bodyless already: it stays in the output
  before this record when the call is allowed, and the rewrite removes both when it is blocked.
  So a custom call that streams in contiguous records after a function call stays conforming.
- The rule is slightly too broad, on purpose: a later fragment that adds nothing
  (`"arguments":""`, `null`, `"function":{}`) is also a deviation. Exempting it adds a case for no
  practical gain.

### 5.2 `choice_without_delta` and `chunk_without_choices` (P-a, P-b, P-f)

While choice 0 has an open call, **and in the record that opens a call of choice 0** (the record
carries tool data for choice 0):

- a chunk with no `choices` key is `Deviation("chunk_without_choices")`;
- a choice entry with no `delta` key, in any position, is `Deviation("choice_without_delta")`.
  One exception: the entry of choice 0 that carries its `finish_reason` may omit `delta`. No
  fragment can follow it (`late_fragment`), so every call is complete when a client raises there.

`"delta": null` stays `Malformed("delta")` in every position (SMA-749 classifier); inside an open
call the queue is non-empty, so it is already a stream-level failure.

Outside an open call these records stay as they are today (classified as tool-free). This limits
the rule to the place where a raise can cut a call.

The record that opens a call counts (P-f): a raise later in that record cuts the call after its
first fragment. One predicate in `stream.rs` (`in_call`: an open call, or this record carries tool
data for choice 0) decides this for § 5.2 and § 5.7, so the two rules cannot drift.

### 5.3 A present `type` key counts as the type fragment (P-c)

`"type": null` is read as "absent" today (`opt_str`, `json.rs`), so a later `"type": null` passes
`repeated_type`. In a tool-call fragment, a present `type` key, `null` included, counts as the type
fragment. A second one is `repeated_type`. A first `"type": null` with a `function` body is
`type_shape_mismatch` at completion. The builder must check that the existing `type`-absent
streams in the fixtures and generators stay conforming.

### 5.4 H1: a top-level `chunk` key

A chunk that has a top-level `chunk` key is `Malformed("chunk_key")` (the record is dropped, with
the same § 6 behaviour of SMA-749 as other malformed records). No real OpenAI-compatible upstream
sends it. The key is added to the classifier key list in `json.rs`, so case-folded forms are
rejected the same way as other classifier keys.

### 5.5 H2: a top-level `type` of `content.delta`

A chunk whose top-level `type` is the string `content.delta` and that carries tool data
(`tool_calls`, `function_call`) or a `finish_reason` is `Malformed("content_delta_type")`.
LangChain skips such a record, so the decider and LangChain would see different calls.

### 5.6 Common consequences

- Real OpenAI did not send any of these shapes in 60 recorded streams (§ 2.4, R1 and R2). So no
  rule fires on that traffic. The recorded fixtures pin this (§ 7.3). A self-hosted or Azure
  upstream that sends one of these shapes gets `on_failure`. The upstream bytes already make at
  least one supported client raise or misread in every case.
- **`"type": null` on every continuation fragment.** An upstream that sends `"type": null` on
  each later fragment of a call (for example a server that dumps pydantic models without
  `exclude_none`) now gets `repeated_type`, so `on_failure` runs on every tool stream from it. The
  rule is necessary: openai-python replaces `type` on such a fragment and its
  `new_tool.type == "function"` assert raises (§ 5.3, P-c). How common this upstream shape is was
  not measured. Real OpenAI does not send it (§ 2.4, R2).
- **Observe mode trade-off.** Under `on_failure = allow`, the deviating record is not emitted and
  later records are forwarded unclassified (SMA-749 § 5.3). A stream that was enforced before (for
  example an interleaved function and custom call) now reaches openai-python and openai-node in
  pass-through, without the deviating record. For P-M3 that record holds the `custom` entry and any
  fragments in it. Observe mode is not a security mode, and every SMA-749 deviation behaves this
  way. This spec does not change that behaviour.
- Each deviation is reported as `RecordDropped("malformed")` and `OnFailure("malformed")`, as the
  existing deviations are. An operator cannot tell the new deviations apart. This is unchanged.
- The rules and their reasons go into the module docs: `src/openai/assembly.rs` for § 5.1 and
  § 5.3, `src/openai/stream.rs` for § 5.2 and § 5.7, and `src/openai/classify.rs` for § 5.4,
  § 5.5 and § 5.8. The SMA-749 spec is not edited; this spec
  supersedes its § 4.3 list for these shapes.

### 5.7 `array_outside_tool_calls` (P-e)

Inside a call of choice 0 (the `in_call` predicate of § 5.2), a delta that holds an array outside
the `tool_calls` array itself is `Deviation("array_outside_tool_calls")`. The array can be the
value of any delta key other than `tool_calls`, or of any key of a tool-call entry, its `function`
and `custom` objects included, or of any key of a legacy `function_call`. It counts at any depth
below those keys. The rule applies to the choice entries in every position of the record, as
§ 5.2 does: a raise in any choice stops openai-python for the whole stream.

- openai-python's `accumulate_delta` merges a list by `index` when the earlier list holds
  non-scalar entries. A later list whose entry is not a dict raises `TypeError`, so the client
  keeps a strict prefix of the call. The rule names the shape (an array where no real upstream
  sends one), not the exact raise condition.
- The rule also covers an array nested in an object (`{"foo":{"bar":[…]}}`), because
  `accumulate_delta` merges dicts recursively. The review named only the first level. A kind
  Other entry with an array in its raw body is a deviation too: that is fail-closed.
- Choice-level keys (for example `logprobs`) are not merged as a delta. They are not checked.
- The recorded streams (§ 2.4) and the conforming fixtures hold no array outside `tool_calls`.
  The recorded delta keys are `content`, `function_call`, `refusal`, `role` and `tool_calls`.
- Outside a call the shape stays conforming: a raise there cuts no call.

### 5.8 `function_call_key` (P-d)

A legacy `function_call` object with a key other than `name` and `arguments` is
`Malformed("function_call_key")`. This applies in every stream record and in a non-stream body:
`classify::legacy_call` reads the object for both.

- LangChain merges the extra key into `additional_kwargs["function_call"]`. When a later fragment
  gives it another JSON type, `merge_dicts` raises `TypeError`. Its snapshot then holds the
  arguments merged so far, which is a strict prefix when more arguments follow.
- The rule is malformed, not a deviation, and it does not depend on an open call: no real OpenAI
  stream or body sends another key (§ 2.4: the recorded `function_call` keys are `name` and
  `arguments`). A body with such a key is `Malformed`, which changes the body path (D4).
- In a stream, the record is dropped. Inside an open hold this is a stream-level failure, as for
  every malformed record (SMA-749 § 6).

## 6. Model changes in the oracle

### 6.1 None for the raise paths

The OpenAI models already raise as the real SDKs do on P-a, P-b, P-c and P-M3 (cited sources in
`oracle.rs`). They are not changed.

### 6.2 LangChain H1 and H2

The LangChain model already reads `chunk.choices` and skips `content.delta` records. It is not
changed.

### 6.3 anthropic-python partial parse

`Partial::value` in `oracle.rs` must drop an unfinished number or literal at the end of the input,
with its key, and not raise, as jiter does (§ 2.3). The doc comment must cite the jiter version
measured. A unit test pins the three measured inputs: `{"n":10.` gives `{}`, `{"n":1e` gives `{}`,
`{"a":"x","n":10.` gives `{"a":"x"}`.

## 7. Tests

### 7.1 Generator quirks

`tests/support/streams.rs` gets one OpenAI `Quirk` for each shape of § 2.2 and § 5: a bodyless
entry interleaved inside an open call (it exists), a chunk without `choices`, a choice entry
without `delta`, a `"type": null` fragment, a top-level `chunk` key with a tool call, a
`content.delta` record with a fragment, two records with an array outside `tool_calls`
(§ 5.7), and two legacy fragments with an extra key that changes type (§ 5.8). The quirk for a choice entry without `delta` also adds `{"index":1}` behind the
record that opens a call (P-f). Each quirk must be able to land between two fragments of
an allowed call. The generators must also emit an Anthropic input with a decimal number, split
inside the number.

### 7.2 A property test of the oracle (the issue's "fails on the current tolerance")

A new proptest drives `check_i1` directly, with no interceptor, on a generated OpenAI stream. It has
an allowed function call 0 whose arguments are split into two fragments, and a raise record from
§ 2.2 (P-M3, P-a, P-b or P-c, chosen by the strategy) between them. `decided` holds the calls, all
`Allow`. The output is the upstream bytes, so the raise is excused and the partial path runs. The
test asserts that `check_i1` returns `Err`, and that the message names the model and call 0.

- On the current oracle it fails: the prefix is accepted.
- After § 4 it passes.

A second case puts the raise record after the last fragment of call 0. The test asserts `Ok`, so
the oracle does not simply reject every excused raise.

`ToolCall` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the test builds the decided calls from `parse_body`
(`BodyCalls.calls`) and changes fields on a clone, or with a test-support constructor if one is
needed. This test lives in one test file (for example `tests/oracle.rs`), not in `support/`,
because `support/` is compiled into every test binary.

### 7.3 Fixtures

One fixture per new rule under `tests/fixtures/openai/malformed/`, generated by
`tests/fixtures/make_fixtures.py`, each with a row in `malformed_shapes_follow_section_6`:
`fragment_after_bodyless_entry`, `chunk_without_choices`, `choice_without_delta`, `type_null`,
`chunk_key`, `content_delta_type`, `array_outside_tool_calls` (§ 5.7),
`choice_without_delta_in_opening_record` (§ 5.2, P-f), `function_call_key` (§ 5.8) and
`fragment_after_blocked_bodyless_entry` (§ 5.1, a renewed boundary). The
conforming fixture `bodyless_type_null` pins a bare `{"index":0,"type":null}` call: kind Other,
named `unknown` by the core and by the oracle.

Each fixture has an **allowed** call (`read_file` with `{"v":"abcdefgh"}`, a function call or a
legacy call for § 5.8) whose fragments are split around the rule's record. The canary is **in
the deviating record itself** (for example a `"note":"CANARY-…"` key), not in a separate
`blocked_*` call: a separate later call is forwarded in observe mode after the deviation, so its
canary would leak there. Then `every_fixture_holds_i1_for_every_client` reds for that fixture
under `allow-all` and `block-by-name` when its rule is removed (§ 7.4). Under `block-all` the
allowed call is blocked and rewritten out, so no partial call reaches a client and I1 cannot red. The H1 fixture puts a `blocked_*` call
inside `chunk`.

The recorded streams of § 2.4 are kept in `openai/recorded`. They are **not** in the fixture sets
of `tests/fixtures.rs` (`SETS`), because the canary and row tests assume the hand-built names.
`recorded_streams_pass_unchanged` replays them with `on_failure = block`:

- One push per file under each of the three deciders (`allow-all`, `block-all`,
  `block-by-name`): the stream ends, there is no `RecordDropped` or `OnFailure` metric, and I1
  holds (`check_i1`). Under `allow-all` the output is also payload-identical to the input, and
  every OpenAI model derives the decided calls from it (the same kinds and names, in order; I1
  compares the arguments).
- Every single split point of every file (one cut), under `allow-all`: the stream ends, the
  metrics are clean, and the output is byte-identical to the one-push output. So it is
  payload-identical to the input, and the client runs of the one-push pass hold for it. The
  files run in parallel threads (about 74 000 drives).

So a future rule that rejects real OpenAI traffic reds at once. `capture.py` stays next to the
recordings, so they can be recorded again. It reads the API key from a file and never prints it.
It is not run in CI.

### 7.4 Proof that each half bites

The plan must record each of these as a measured red. Each mutation must compile (`-D warnings`
applies to test targets) and is reverted by deleting the marked edit, not by `git checkout`.

1. The § 7.2 test, written first, against the current oracle. (Red 1 is the same state as
   mutation 3 below: the prefix branch exists. Measure it once, before § 4.)
2. `every_fixture_holds_i1_for_every_client` with § 4 and the § 7.3 fixtures, before § 5. Every
   new fixture must red, by name. This is deterministic, unlike a random P1 run.
3. After all changes: restore the prefix acceptance in `arguments_match`. The § 7.2 test must red.
4. After all changes: delete each § 5 rule in turn. Its fixture must red in
   `every_fixture_holds_i1_for_every_client`, not only in the `stream_failure` column.
5. After all changes: restore the raising `Partial` behaviour. The § 6.3 unit test must red.

`openai_p1_and_p2_hold` and `anthropic_p1_and_p2_hold` must pass at 10 000 cases after all
changes. A random red in them before § 5 is expected but is not part of the proof.

## 8. Changes to the test deciders

None are needed for the proof: D2 is decider-free. The existing three deciders stay.

## 9. Non-goals

- `json.rs` `DATA_KEYS` matches `input`, `input_schema` and `parameters` by key name only. That is
  safe while no classifier reads below those keys. SMA-750 or SMA-752 must re-check it when one
  does. This change does not touch it.
- Kind `other` arguments are not compared (§ 4). An SMA-752 policy that reads them needs its own
  rule.
- A BOM-prefixed first record that openai-python ignores on the upstream bytes reaches it after the
  SMA-749 D2 BOM strip. With a chunk that has no `choices`, the client then raises. This is
  availability only: no tool call is affected (a hidden first record with a call makes the client
  run fewer calls). It is SMA-749 behaviour, and this change does not fix it. The generator keeps
  such records off the first line when it emits a BOM.
- No change to the Anthropic assembly, to bodies (except § 5.8), or to the decider port
  (`ToolCallDecider`).
- The OpenAI Responses API (`/v1/responses`) is SMA-769, which starts after this change. It needs
  its own ingress, format and oracle models. It takes the D2 rule and the recording method of this
  spec from the start (§ 2.4).
- Support for an upstream that sends `"type": null` on every continuation fragment (§ 5.6). It
  gets `on_failure`; this change does not measure or relax that.
- The LangChain model is `<not pinned: modelled only>` (`oracle.rs`). This change does not pin it.
  If the real SDK does not raise where the model raises, the § 5 rules still hold: they only reject
  streams.

## 10. Left to the builder

- The exact doc-comment text, the proptest strategies, and the fixture contents within § 7.3.
- Whether a test-support constructor for `ToolCall` is needed (§ 7.2).
- The exact place of each § 5 check in `Check::apply` or the classifier, within the rule that
  every check runs on the copy before anything changes.

from __future__ import annotations

import inspect
from types import TracebackType
from typing import Any, List, Generic, Iterable, Awaitable, cast
from typing_extensions import Self, Callable, Iterator, AsyncIterator

from ._types import ParsedResponseSnapshot
from ._events import (
    ResponseStreamEvent,
    ResponseTextDoneEvent,
    ResponseCompletedEvent,
    ResponseTextDeltaEvent,
    ResponseFunctionCallArgumentsDeltaEvent,
)
from ...._types import Omit, omit
from ...._utils import is_given, consume_sync_iterator, consume_async_iterator
from ...._compat import PYDANTIC_V1, model_copy
from ...._models import build, construct_type_unchecked
from ...._streaming import Stream, AsyncStream
from ....types.responses import (
    ParsedResponse,
    ResponseStreamEvent as RawResponseStreamEvent,
    ResponseOutputItemDoneEvent,
    ResponseOutputItemAddedEvent,
)
from ..._parsing._responses import TextFormatT, parse_text, parse_response
from ....types.responses.tool_param import ToolParam
from ....types.responses.parsed_response import (
    ParsedContent,
    ParsedResponseOutputItem,
    ParsedResponseOutputMessage,
    ParsedResponseFunctionToolCall,
)
from ....types.responses.response_output_item import ResponseOutputItem


class ResponseStream(Generic[TextFormatT]):
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        raw_stream: Stream[RawResponseStreamEvent],
        text_format: type[TextFormatT] | Omit,
        input_tools: Iterable[ToolParam] | Omit,
        starting_after: int | None,
    ) -> None:
        self._raw_stream = raw_stream
        self._response = raw_stream.response
        self._iterator = self.__stream__()
        self._state = ResponseStreamState(text_format=text_format, input_tools=input_tools)
        self._starting_after = starting_after

    def __next__(self) -> ResponseStreamEvent[TextFormatT]:
        return self._iterator.__next__()

    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[ResponseStreamEvent[TextFormatT]]:
        for item in self._iterator:
            yield item

    def __enter__(self) -> Self:
        return self

    def __stream__(self) -> Iterator[ResponseStreamEvent[TextFormatT]]:
        for sse_event in self._raw_stream:
            events_to_fire = self._state.handle_event(sse_event)
            for event in events_to_fire:
                if self._starting_after is None or event.sequence_number > self._starting_after:
                    yield event

    def __exit__(
        self,
        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
        exc: BaseException | None,
        exc_tb: TracebackType | None,
    ) -> None:
        self.close()

    def close(self) -> None:
        """
        Close the response and release the connection.

        Automatically called if the response body is read to completion.
        """
        self._response.close()

    def get_final_response(self) -> ParsedResponse[TextFormatT]:
        """Waits until the stream has been read to completion and returns
        the accumulated `ParsedResponse` object.
        """
        self.until_done()
        response = self._state._completed_response
        if not response:
            raise RuntimeError("Didn't receive a `response.completed` event.")

        return response

    def until_done(self) -> Self:
        """Blocks until the stream has been consumed."""
        consume_sync_iterator(self)
        return self


class ResponseStreamManager(Generic[TextFormatT]):
    def __init__(
        self,
        api_request: Callable[[], Stream[RawResponseStreamEvent]],
        *,
        text_format: type[TextFormatT] | Omit,
        input_tools: Iterable[ToolParam] | Omit,
        starting_after: int | None,
    ) -> None:
        self.__stream: ResponseStream[TextFormatT] | None = None
        self.__api_request = api_request
        self.__text_format = text_format
        self.__input_tools = input_tools
        self.__starting_after = starting_after

    def __enter__(self) -> ResponseStream[TextFormatT]:
        raw_stream = self.__api_request()

        self.__stream = ResponseStream(
            raw_stream=raw_stream,
            text_format=self.__text_format,
            input_tools=self.__input_tools,
            starting_after=self.__starting_after,
        )

        return self.__stream

    def __exit__(
        self,
        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
        exc: BaseException | None,
        exc_tb: TracebackType | None,
    ) -> None:
        if self.__stream is not None:
            self.__stream.close()


class AsyncResponseStream(Generic[TextFormatT]):
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        raw_stream: AsyncStream[RawResponseStreamEvent],
        text_format: type[TextFormatT] | Omit,
        input_tools: Iterable[ToolParam] | Omit,
        starting_after: int | None,
    ) -> None:
        self._raw_stream = raw_stream
        self._response = raw_stream.response
        self._iterator = self.__stream__()
        self._state = ResponseStreamState(text_format=text_format, input_tools=input_tools)
        self._starting_after = starting_after

    async def __anext__(self) -> ResponseStreamEvent[TextFormatT]:
        return await self._iterator.__anext__()

    async def __aiter__(self) -> AsyncIterator[ResponseStreamEvent[TextFormatT]]:
        async for item in self._iterator:
            yield item

    async def __stream__(self) -> AsyncIterator[ResponseStreamEvent[TextFormatT]]:
        async for sse_event in self._raw_stream:
            events_to_fire = self._state.handle_event(sse_event)
            for event in events_to_fire:
                if self._starting_after is None or event.sequence_number > self._starting_after:
                    yield event

    async def __aenter__(self) -> Self:
        return self

    async def __aexit__(
        self,
        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
        exc: BaseException | None,
        exc_tb: TracebackType | None,
    ) -> None:
        await self.close()

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """
        Close the response and release the connection.

        Automatically called if the response body is read to completion.
        """
        await self._response.aclose()

    async def get_final_response(self) -> ParsedResponse[TextFormatT]:
        """Waits until the stream has been read to completion and returns
        the accumulated `ParsedResponse` object.
        """
        await self.until_done()
        response = self._state._completed_response
        if not response:
            raise RuntimeError("Didn't receive a `response.completed` event.")

        return response

    async def until_done(self) -> Self:
        """Blocks until the stream has been consumed."""
        await consume_async_iterator(self)
        return self


class AsyncResponseStreamManager(Generic[TextFormatT]):
    def __init__(
        self,
        api_request: Awaitable[AsyncStream[RawResponseStreamEvent]],
        *,
        text_format: type[TextFormatT] | Omit,
        input_tools: Iterable[ToolParam] | Omit,
        starting_after: int | None,
    ) -> None:
        self.__stream: AsyncResponseStream[TextFormatT] | None = None
        self.__api_request = api_request
        self.__text_format = text_format
        self.__input_tools = input_tools
        self.__starting_after = starting_after

    async def __aenter__(self) -> AsyncResponseStream[TextFormatT]:
        raw_stream = await self.__api_request

        self.__stream = AsyncResponseStream(
            raw_stream=raw_stream,
            text_format=self.__text_format,
            input_tools=self.__input_tools,
            starting_after=self.__starting_after,
        )

        return self.__stream

    async def __aexit__(
        self,
        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
        exc: BaseException | None,
        exc_tb: TracebackType | None,
    ) -> None:
        if self.__stream is not None:
            await self.__stream.close()


def _output_identity(
    item: ResponseOutputItem | ParsedResponseOutputItem[object],
) -> tuple[str, str | None, str | None]:
    call_id = getattr(item, "call_id", None)
    if item.type in ("function_call", "custom_tool_call", "shell_call", "shell_call_output"):
        return item.type, None, call_id
    return item.type, getattr(item, "id", None), call_id


def _compatible_output_id(
    previous: ResponseOutputItem | ParsedResponseOutputItem[object], replacement: ResponseOutputItem
) -> bool:
    previous_id = getattr(previous, "id", None)
    return previous_id == getattr(replacement, "id", None) or (
        previous_id is None and previous.type in ("function_call", "custom_tool_call")
    )


class ResponseStreamState(Generic[TextFormatT]):
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        input_tools: Iterable[ToolParam] | Omit,
        text_format: type[TextFormatT] | Omit,
    ) -> None:
        self.__current_snapshot: ParsedResponseSnapshot | None = None
        self._completed_response: ParsedResponse[TextFormatT] | None = None
        self._completed_output: dict[int, ResponseOutputItem] = {}
        self._completed_positions: dict[tuple[str, str | None, str | None], int] = {}
        self._output_items: dict[int, ParsedResponseOutputItem[object]] = {}
        self._input_tools = [tool for tool in input_tools] if is_given(input_tools) else []
        self._text_format = text_format
        self._rich_text_format: type | Omit = text_format if inspect.isclass(text_format) else omit

    def handle_event(self, event: RawResponseStreamEvent) -> List[ResponseStreamEvent[TextFormatT]]:
        if event.type == "response.output_item.added":
            event = construct_type_unchecked(
                type_=ResponseOutputItemAddedEvent,
                value={
                    **vars(event),
                    **cast("dict[str, Any]", {} if PYDANTIC_V1 else (getattr(event, "__pydantic_extra__", None) or {})),
                    "item": getattr(event, "item", None),
                    "output_index": event.output_index,
                },
            )
        elif event.type == "response.output_item.done":
            event = construct_type_unchecked(
                type_=ResponseOutputItemDoneEvent,
                value={
                    **vars(event),
                    **cast("dict[str, Any]", {} if PYDANTIC_V1 else (getattr(event, "__pydantic_extra__", None) or {})),
                    "item": event.item,
                    "output_index": event.output_index,
                },
            )
        self.__current_snapshot = self.accumulate_event(event)

        events: List[ResponseStreamEvent[TextFormatT]] = []

        if event.type == "response.output_item.added" and getattr(event, "item", None) is None:
            return events
        elif event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
            output = self._get_output_item(event.output_index)
            assert output.type == "message"

            content = output.content[event.content_index]
            assert content.type == "output_text"

            events.append(
                build(
                    ResponseTextDeltaEvent,
                    content_index=event.content_index,
                    delta=event.delta,
                    item_id=event.item_id,
                    output_index=event.output_index,
                    sequence_number=event.sequence_number,
                    logprobs=event.logprobs,
                    type="response.output_text.delta",
                    snapshot=content.text,
                )
            )
        elif event.type == "response.output_text.done":
            output = self._get_output_item(event.output_index)
            assert output.type == "message"

            content = output.content[event.content_index]
            assert content.type == "output_text"

            events.append(
                build(
                    cast("type[ResponseTextDoneEvent[TextFormatT]]", ResponseTextDoneEvent),
                    content_index=event.content_index,
                    item_id=event.item_id,
                    output_index=event.output_index,
                    sequence_number=event.sequence_number,
                    logprobs=event.logprobs,
                    type="response.output_text.done",
                    text=event.text,
                    parsed=parse_text(event.text, text_format=self._text_format, phase=output.phase),
                )
            )
        elif event.type == "response.function_call_arguments.delta":
            output = self._get_output_item(event.output_index)
            assert output.type == "function_call"

            events.append(
                build(
                    ResponseFunctionCallArgumentsDeltaEvent,
                    delta=event.delta,
                    item_id=event.item_id,
                    output_index=event.output_index,
                    sequence_number=event.sequence_number,
                    type="response.function_call_arguments.delta",
                    snapshot=output.arguments,
                )
            )

        elif event.type == "response.completed":
            response = self._completed_response
            assert response is not None

            events.append(
                build(
                    ResponseCompletedEvent,
                    sequence_number=event.sequence_number,
                    type="response.completed",
                    response=response,
                )
            )
        elif (
            event.type == "response.created"
            or event.type == "response.queued"
            or event.type == "response.in_progress"
            or event.type == "response.failed"
            or event.type == "response.incomplete"
        ):
            if getattr(event.response, "output", None) is None:
                event = model_copy(event, deep=True)
                event.response.output = (
                    [
                        cast(
                            ResponseOutputItem,
                            model_copy(
                                self._completed_output[index]
                                if index in self._completed_output
                                else self._output_items[index],
                                deep=True,
                            ),
                        )
                        for index in sorted(self._output_items.keys() | self._completed_output.keys())
                    ]
                    if event.type == "response.failed" or event.type == "response.incomplete"
                    else []
                )
            events.append(event)
        else:
            events.append(event)

        return events

    def accumulate_event(self, event: RawResponseStreamEvent) -> ParsedResponseSnapshot:
        snapshot = self.__current_snapshot
        if snapshot is None:
            return self._create_initial_response(event)

        if (
            event.type == "response.created"
            or event.type == "response.queued"
            or event.type == "response.in_progress"
            or event.type == "response.completed"
            or event.type == "response.failed"
            or event.type == "response.incomplete"
        ) and getattr(event.response, "id", None) != getattr(snapshot, "id", None):
            raise RuntimeError("Lifecycle response identity changed.")

        if event.type == "response.created" or event.type == "response.queued" or event.type == "response.in_progress":
            replacements: dict[tuple[str, str | None, str | None], ResponseOutputItem] = {}
            lifecycle_output = cast("list[ResponseOutputItem] | None", getattr(event.response, "output", None))
            for replacement_item in lifecycle_output or []:
                identity = _output_identity(replacement_item)
                if identity in replacements:
                    raise RuntimeError("Response snapshot has conflicting output identities.")
                replacements[identity] = replacement_item
            for updated_identity, replacement in replacements.items():
                index = self._completed_positions.get(updated_identity)
                if index is not None:
                    if not _compatible_output_id(self._completed_output[index], replacement):
                        raise RuntimeError("Response snapshot has conflicting output identities.")
                    self._completed_output[index] = model_copy(replacement, deep=True)
        elif event.type == "response.output_item.added":
            if getattr(event, "item", None) is None:
                return snapshot
            if event.output_index in self._output_items:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Duplicate response output index {event.output_index}.")

            if event.item.type == "function_call":
                snapshot.output.append(
                    construct_type_unchecked(
                        type_=cast(Any, ParsedResponseFunctionToolCall), value=event.item.to_dict()
                    )
                )
            elif event.item.type == "message":
                snapshot.output.append(
                    construct_type_unchecked(type_=cast(Any, ParsedResponseOutputMessage), value=event.item.to_dict())
                )
            else:
                snapshot.output.append(event.item)
            self._output_items[event.output_index] = snapshot.output[-1]
        elif event.type == "response.content_part.added":
            output = self._get_output_item(event.output_index)
            if output.type == "message":
                output.content.append(
                    construct_type_unchecked(type_=cast(Any, ParsedContent), value=event.part.to_dict())
                )
        elif event.type == "response.output_text.delta":
            output = self._get_output_item(event.output_index)
            if output.type == "message":
                content = output.content[event.content_index]
                assert content.type == "output_text"
                content.text += event.delta
        elif event.type == "response.function_call_arguments.delta":
            output = self._get_output_item(event.output_index)
            if output.type == "function_call":
                output.arguments += event.delta
        elif event.type == "response.output_item.done":
            added = self._output_items.get(event.output_index)
            if added is not None and (
                _output_identity(added) != _output_identity(event.item) or not _compatible_output_id(added, event.item)
            ):
                raise RuntimeError("Completed output item identity changed.")
            identity = _output_identity(event.item)
            position = self._completed_positions.get(identity)
            if position is not None and position != event.output_index:
                raise RuntimeError("Response snapshot has conflicting output identities.")
            previous = self._completed_output.get(event.output_index)
            if previous is not None:
                del self._completed_positions[_output_identity(previous)]
            self._completed_output[event.output_index] = event.item
            self._completed_positions[identity] = event.output_index
        elif event.type == "response.completed":
            response = event.response
            final_output = cast("list[ResponseOutputItem] | None", getattr(response, "output", None))
            final_items = {_output_identity(item): item for item in (final_output or [])}
            for completed_item in self._completed_output.values():
                final_completed_item = final_items.get(_output_identity(completed_item))
                if final_completed_item is not None and not _compatible_output_id(completed_item, final_completed_item):
                    raise RuntimeError("Completed response output identity changed.")
            for index, item in self._output_items.items():
                final_item = final_items.get(_output_identity(item))
                if index not in self._completed_output and (
                    final_item is None or not _compatible_output_id(item, final_item)
                ):
                    raise RuntimeError("Cannot complete response with unfinished output items.")
            if getattr(response, "output", None) is None:
                # Recover finalized items; deltas can omit final status, annotations, or refusals.
                response = model_copy(response)
                response.output = [self._completed_output[index] for index in sorted(self._completed_output)]
            self._completed_response = parse_response(
                text_format=self._text_format,
                response=response,
                input_tools=self._input_tools,
            )

        return snapshot

    def _get_output_item(self, output_index: int) -> ParsedResponseOutputItem[object]:
        try:
            return self._output_items[output_index]
        except KeyError:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Received a content event for output index {output_index} before receiving its output item"
            ) from None

    def _create_initial_response(self, event: RawResponseStreamEvent) -> ParsedResponseSnapshot:
        if event.type != "response.created":
            raise RuntimeError(f"Expected to have received `response.created` before `{event.type}`")

        snapshot = construct_type_unchecked(type_=ParsedResponseSnapshot, value=event.response.to_dict())
        # Stream indexes can have gaps when a provider emits an empty added event.
        if getattr(snapshot, "output", None) is None:
            snapshot.output = []
        self._output_items = dict(enumerate(snapshot.output))
        return snapshot

308	class _SSELineDecoder:
309	    """Incrementally split CR, LF, and CRLF without copying growing prefixes."""
310	
311	    def __init__(self) -> None:
312	        self._buffer = bytearray()
313	        self._skip_lf = False
314	
315	    def _append(self, chunk: bytes, start: int, end: int) -> None:
316	        self._buffer.extend(memoryview(chunk)[start:end])
317	
318	    def feed(self, chunk: bytes) -> Iterator[bytes]:
319	        start = 0
320	        for match in _SSE_LINE_END.finditer(chunk):
321	            end = match.start()
322	            if self._skip_lf and end == start and chunk[end] == 10:
323	                self._skip_lf = False
324	                start = end + 1
325	                continue
326	            self._skip_lf = False
327	            self._append(chunk, start, end)
328	            line = bytes(self._buffer)
329	            self._buffer.clear()
330	            self._skip_lf = chunk[end] == 13
331	            start = end + 1
332	            yield line
333	        if start < len(chunk):
334	            self._skip_lf = False
335	            self._append(chunk, start, len(chunk))
336	
337	    def finish(self) -> Iterator[bytes]:
338	        if self._buffer:
339	            line = bytes(self._buffer)
340	            self._buffer.clear()
341	            yield line

393	            if not self._event and not self._data and not self._last_event_id and self._retry is None:
394	                return None
395	
396	            sse = ServerSentEvent(
397	                event=self._event,
398	                data="\n".join(self._data),
399	                id=self._last_event_id,
400	                retry=self._retry,
401	            )
402	
403	            # NOTE: as per the SSE spec, do not reset last_event_id.
404	            self._event = None
405	            self._data = []
406	            self._retry = None
407	
408	            return sse
409	
410	        if line.startswith(":"):
411	            return None
412	
413	        fieldname, _, value = line.partition(":")
414

## Verdict: NEEDS REWORK
The architecture is sound: a separate format module, one hold per item, stateless only, and a replacement at the same index. But the canonical rules let a tool-free index become an undecided tool call in all three SDKs. Billing cannot read usage from a large terminal event. The oracle does not compare arguments for the six new kinds, and the § 5.5 rewrite does not cover most of the items it must rewrite.

## Findings

Paths: `rs/…` and `py/…` are under `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-core-sma-769/`. `base.py`, `ai.py`, `json.py` (LangChain) and `*.mjs` (openai-node) are under `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-smaschek-dev-paigasus-paigasus-core/1897327f-fffc-4b34-860d-d276c6197223/scratchpad/sdk-src/`. `_responses.py` and `_streaming.py` are in `py/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/openai/`.

### BLOCKER

- **The item class is not fixed across views for tool-free items (I1 break)** - R8 (type, id, call_id, name equality) applies only to tool-bearing items. § 5.4 says "Tool-free and provider-run items need R4 to R7, R12 and R13 only". The class is fixed at `added`, so an index that is added as `message` (or `reasoning`, or `web_search_call`) and then arrives as a `custom_tool_call` at `done`, or as a `function_call` in the terminal `response.output`, goes out unheld. Evidence from the sources:
  - LangChain makes a tool call from any `output_item.done` whose item type is `custom_tool_call`. It never checks the `added` type (`base.py:5615-5631`). Built-in kinds become content blocks the same way (`base.py:5596-5614`).
  - openai-python `ResponseStream` does not raise when the terminal item at a completed index has another identity. The `final_completed_item is not None` guard skips it (`_responses.py:484-494`), and `get_final_response()` returns the new call.
  - openai-node `#assertComplete` skips an item it cannot find (`ResponseStream.mjs:244-250`). `cloneValidatedResponse` then makes the terminal output the snapshot.
  - R12's "A `response.output` item that never streamed" can mean per index or per identity, so two builders can build it differently.
  - Event level: § 5.3 makes an item-scoped event tool-bearing or tool-free by its item, but no rule binds an event type to an item type. A `response.function_call_arguments.delta` inside a `custom_tool_call` item reaches LangChain as an extra `tool_call_chunk` at the same index. LangChain joins the args, and `parse_partial_json` keeps the first complete object (`json.py:129-145`). So the stray `{"__arg1":"rm -rf /"}` plus the decided `{"__arg1":"ls"}` runs `rm -rf /`.
  - The same event on a `message` item gives LangChain a call named `""` (`ai.py:557-561`).
  | Why it matters: All three supported parsers can run a call that no decider saw, or other arguments than the decider saw, under T2. The § 9.3 quirk list does not generate these shapes, so P1 would not find them. | Suggested fix: (1) Apply R8 to every item. The terminal item at each index has the same `type` and `id` as the streamed item, and a tool-bearing terminal item equals its `done` item. (2) Add a closed map from each item-scoped event type to its one item type. Use Node's `expectedOutputItemTypes` (`response-accumulator.mjs:111-153`), plus `content_part.*` → `message`/`reasoning` and `shell_call_command.*` → `shell_call`. A mismatch is malformed. (3) `added.item` must be an object with a string `type`. `item: null` is malformed, because both SDKs skip it (`_responses.py:432`, `ResponseStream.mjs:215`). (4) Add a generator quirk for each case.

- **D13 billing cannot read usage from a large terminal event** - `UsageScanner` skips any record over `MAX_RECORD_BYTES = 64 * 1024` and never parses it (`rs/.../paigasus-gateway/src/adapters/http/usage.rs:11`, `:122-126`). Every Responses lifecycle event carries the whole `response` object. That object holds the echoed `instructions` and `tools`, and in `response.completed` every output item again (text, arguments, encrypted reasoning). An agent with a long system prompt and many tool schemas can pass 64 KiB. I did not measure the sizes. Then `reported` stays `None`, and `ChargeGuard` charges the request estimate plus one token per record (`application/charge_guard.rs:124`). This happens with interception on or off. The fallbacks are also undefined for Responses: `non_stream_usage` reads only `choices[]` (`usage.rs:65`), and the D13 request estimate has no defined shape, but it would become the common path. | Why it matters: Large responses would be undercharged by large factors. The budget limits (AC 1) would not hold. | Suggested fix: Specify a Responses usage reader that gets `response.usage` with no 64 KiB buffer limit, for example a bounded streaming scan for the `usage` key of `response`. Add service tests with terminal events over 64 KiB and over 1 MiB. Specify the request estimate (`instructions`, `input` string, each input item type) and the body fallback (`output[].content[].text`, `arguments`) as precisely as the chat D14 rule.

- **The oracle does not compare arguments for the six new kinds** - `kind_of` maps every kind it does not list to `"other"` (`rs/.../paigasus-gateway-core/tests/support/oracle.rs:89-97`). `arguments_match` returns `true` for `"other"` (`:118-121`). § 5.1 gives Computer, LocalShell, Shell, ApplyPatch, ToolSearch and McpApprovalRequest the same decided form as Other (the raw `done` item). § 9.1 does not say how to compare them. | Why it matters: P1 cannot fail on a wrong shell command, patch diff or computer action. D15 calls these the most dangerous kinds. The proof for them would pass with nothing checked. | Suggested fix: Give each new kind its own model kind and a defined comparison. For example, compare the item as JSON with `status` removed, after the normalisation each SDK applies (LangChain uses `model_dump(exclude_none=True)`, `base.py:5612`). Add a mutation proof: a changed `action.commands` in the `done` item must make P1 fail.

### MAJOR

- **The strict envelope rules reject echoed request data** - Lifecycle events and non-stream bodies echo `text.format.schema`, `metadata`, `tools[]` (outside `parameters`) and `instructions`. Only `input`, `input_schema` and `parameters` get the data rules (`rs/.../paigasus-gateway-core/src/json.rs:105`). A structured-output property such as `"Name"`, `"ID"` or `"Type"`, a metadata key `"Id"`, or a property `constructor` makes `response.created` and `response.completed` `case_folded_key` or `prototype_key` (`json.rs:73-85`). The body path runs `check_numbers` over the whole body (`src/body.rs:36`), so a schema `"maximum": 1e300` gives `lossy_number` and a 502. | Why it matters: Common structured-output requests fail. A dropped `response.created` makes Python and Node raise at the next event. With a hold open, the failure blocks every tool call. | Suggested fix: Add per-format data subtrees for Responses: `response.text`, `response.metadata`, `response.tools`, `response.instructions` and `response.prompt`. Apply `check_numbers` only to tool-bearing items. Add fixtures. Also decide whether the new keys (`output_index`, `item_id`, `call_id`, `item`, `output`, …) join `CLASSIFIER_KEYS`. A global list would change chat behaviour (AC 8), so make it per format.

- **The record size limits break ordinary Responses traffic** - The interceptor treats a record over `max_record_bytes` (1 MiB) as a stream failure even with an empty queue (`src/interceptor.rs:234-237`). Long `instructions` repeat in `response.created`, `response.in_progress` and `response.completed`. `image_generation_call` items and `partial_image` events carry base64 images. `response.completed` repeats the whole output. | Why it matters: Every SDK then raises, because there is no `response.created` or no `response.completed`. This also happens on text-only streams. | Suggested fix: State a size model for Responses. Either use a larger cap for lifecycle events, or do not parse the `instructions`, `tools` and image `result` subtrees. Add a test above 1 MiB. Also review `max_request_bytes` (1 MiB default, `paigasus-gateway/src/config.rs:438`). D3 makes clients resend the whole conversation, with encrypted reasoning, on every turn.

- **The § 5.5 rewrite does not cover most blocked items** - The rewrite has five gaps:
  - "A blocked item always has at least three frames" is false. The 3.48.0 union has no progress event for `computer_call`, `apply_patch_call`, `local_shell_call`, `mcp_approval_request` or `tool_search_call`. With R5 and R13, their only frames are `added` and `done` (k = 2). With k = 2, strictly increasing numbers for four events are impossible.
  - Some items are blocked while they assemble: on `HoldLimit`, on a stream failure, or when a hold opens in `Mode::Failed` (`interceptor.rs:285-291`). Their frames are released one by one, and the spec defines no events for this case.
  - A truncated item has no `done` frame.
  - In the k = 3 case, LangChain never sees the notice. LangChain reads text only from `output_text.delta` (`base.py:5492`).
  - For a truncated item, R12 ("equals the done item") cannot hold. The terminal event then becomes a deviation and is dropped instead of rewritten.
  | Why it matters: An implementer must invent the common case. A wrong choice makes Node raise or drops the terminal event. | Suggested fix: Define the rewrite per frame:
  - The item's `added` frame becomes the replacement `added`, `content_part.added` and `output_text.delta`.
  - The middle frames are dropped.
  - The item's `done` frame becomes the replacement `done`. When no `done` arrives, synthesize one before the terminal event, `[DONE]`, EOF or the D12 frame, as chat's `closing()` does.
  - Always replace the terminal item at a blocked index, and exempt it from R12.
  - Drop the strict sequence rule, or allow repeated numbers. No SDK reads `sequence_number` for `create`.
  - Give the exact JSON of each event: `item_id`, `output_index`, `content_index: 0`, `logprobs: []` and `annotations: []`. Node raises when `item_id` is missing (`response-accumulator.mjs:201-208`).

- **R11 contradicts itself for `shell_call`, and assumes built-ins are complete at `added`** - R11 requires `added` = `done` except `status`, and it also allows `response.shell_call_command.*`. Node builds `action.commands` from those events, starting from the `added` item (`response-accumulator.mjs:664-683`). So a streamed shell call has different `action.commands` in `added` and `done`. "Their concatenated text" is ambiguous: `commands` is an array keyed by `command_index`, and those events have no `item_id`. Nothing measures whether `apply_patch_call` or `computer_call` arrive complete at `added`. | Why it matters: R11 either blocks every streamed shell call, or implementers guess. If the `added` items are partial, R11 blocks every apply_patch and computer call. | Suggested fix: State the rule per command index: `added.command` plus the deltas equal `done.command`, which equals `done.item.action.commands[i]`, and indexes append in order. Leave `action.commands` out of the `added` = `done` comparison. Add a measurement of the `added` and `done` shapes of each client-run built-in kind.

- **The recordings cannot test the rules that real traffic may break** - § 9.4 records functions, custom tools, reasoning and text only. Nothing records built-in or provider-run tools, a long reasoning run (keepalives), a `max_output_tokens` cut inside a call, `response.failed`, an `error` event, a terminal event over 64 KiB, or structured output. LangChain's source says that real traffic breaks R4/R6: "After several built-in tool calls the API can report a later `output_index` on an item's `done` events than on its `added` event" (`base.py:5419-5421`). Other unmeasured lifecycle shapes can also red whole streams:
  - A `keepalive` without `sequence_number` fails R7 ("every event has it or none").
  - A first `error` event fails R1.
  - A `[DONE]` after the terminal event is dropped as `after_done`, which reds `recorded_streams_pass_unchanged`.
  | Why it matters: A deviation sets `Mode::Failed`, which blocks every later hold in the stream. Long reasoning streams with gpt-6.1-sol, the target of § 1, are the most exposed. | Suggested fix: Add these scenarios to `capture.py` and to the M-list. Exempt `keepalive` and `error` from R1 and R7, or measure them first. Define what happens to `[DONE]` after a terminal event.

- **The next turn after a rewrite is not measured** - Under D3 the client sends the rewritten output back as `input`. In a reasoning model's output, a `reasoning` item often comes directly before the `function_call`. After the rewrite, `msg_paigasus_<i>` follows that reasoning item instead. I recall a known OpenAI 400 for a reasoning item "provided without its required following item", but this is not measured here. The `msg_paigasus_` id might also fail OpenAI's input id checks. | Why it matters: If OpenAI rejects it, every block breaks the agent loop on the next turn, for exactly the models of § 1. | Suggested fix: Add a measurement that replays a rewritten output as `input`, with and without `store`, with `encrypted_content`. Settle the rewrite before implementation. One option is to also drop the preceding `reasoning` item.

- **`ToolCall` drops identity fields that clients dispatch on** - `function_call` has `namespace`, `caller` and `async` (`types/responses/response_function_tool_call.py:50-57`). openai-python finds the tool by `(namespace, name)` (`lib/_parsing/_responses.py:170-189`). LangChain keeps `namespace` (`base.py:5587-5588`). `mcp_approval_request` is identified by `server_label` plus `name`. § 5.1 gives the decider only `name`. | Why it matters: An SMA-752 policy, the report and the notice cannot tell `fs.delete` from `db.delete`. | Suggested fix: Add `namespace`/`server_label` to the decided identity, as a field or a qualified name. Compare them in R8 and in the oracle. Read `namespace` tools into `TurnFacts.definitions`.

- **`TurnFacts.definitions` can be incomplete in the way D3 gives as a reason to refuse `prompt`** - D3 refuses `prompt` because a template "can add tools that the gateway cannot see". `tool_search` (deferred tools, `tool_search_output`) and `additional_tools` items add tools inside a stateless request too. | Why it matters: The reasoning is not consistent. Definition-based policies fail open or closed, with no rule to say which. | Suggested fix: Mark the turn as having incomplete definitions when these tools are used, or read `additional_tools`/`tool_search_output` as definitions. State the rule.

- **The client models do not count everything a client runs** - The models have five gaps:
  - The LangChain model counts only `tool_calls`. LangChain exposes `computer_call`, `apply_patch_call`, `mcp_approval_request` and `tool_search_call` as content blocks (`base.py:5596-5614`).
  - The Python model ignores `event.response.output` of a yielded `response.incomplete` or `response.failed`, and the complete `added` items of built-in kinds.
  - No model covers the plain `client.responses.create(stream=True)` consumer. That consumer is common and never raises, so the excused-raise path makes the `ResponseStream` model weaker than it.
  - `check_i1` matches by choice, kind, name and arguments, not by `output_index` or `call_id` (`oracle.rs:158`). I1 names the output index.
  - `runners()` falls back to the chat runners with `_ =>` (`oracle.rs:81-85`). If the Responses arm is missing, the tests run with zero calls and pass.
  | Why it matters: P1 can pass while a client runs a call. | Suggested fix: Extend the models and add a raw-stream model. Match by `position` and `call_id` too, or remove "output index" from I1. Make the wildcard arm panic. Add the missing quirks: an item type change, an event on the wrong item type, a duplicate `id` or `call_id`, `item: null`, a top-level `error` key, `[DONE]x`, and a non-empty `in_progress.output`.

- **R9 contradicts the chat ruling on empty arguments** - R9 says "the decider sees `""`, as in chat". Chat presents `""` as `"{}"` (749 § 11, `src/openai/assembly.rs:247-248`), and the oracle already matches `""` against `"{}"` (`oracle.rs:133`). | Why it matters: The SMA-752 decider would get two forms of one call, one per format. | Suggested fix: Keep the chat rule (`""` becomes `"{}"`) and correct R9.

- **No route switch and no rollback path** - `/v1/responses` goes live on upgrade for every caller with `InvokeModel` (`adapters/http/auth.rs:68`). `[tool_interception]` turns on for both routes at once. | Why it matters: Billing and availability depend on shapes that nobody has measured yet (see the D13 billing blocker and the record-size finding). An operator cannot turn the route off without a new deploy. | Suggested fix: Add a config flag for the route, off by default or on with interception off. Document the rollback.

### MINOR

- **§ 3.2 counts** - The openai-python 3.48.0 `ResponseStreamEvent` union has 59 members, not 60 (`types/responses/response_stream_event.py:71-129`). With `keepalive` it has 60, which equals Node's set (`response-accumulator.mjs:242-303`). Node ignores 11 types, not six. | Why it matters: The spec states the count as a fact. | Suggested fix: Correct the counts. Also record that a truthy top-level `error` key raises in openai-python (`_streaming.py:95`) and in Node (`core/streaming.mjs:122`).
- **DTO fields** - § 6 does not say whether `model` and `input` are optional. | Why it matters: If they are required, `prompt`-only and `previous_response_id`-only requests get a 400 with interception off, which breaks D3's "plain proxy". | Suggested fix: Make both fields `Option`.
- **New error code** - `responses-stateful-not-supported` needs the chain that 749 § 7 listed: proto, codegen drift, `GatewayError`, `ci/error-registry/check.py` and the SDK `mapError`. | Why it matters: The plan will miss gate work. | Suggested fix: Add a repo-gates section.
