## Verdict: NEEDS REWORK
The architecture is sound: a separate format module, one hold per item, stateless only, and a replacement at the same index. But the canonical rules let a tool-free index become an undecided tool call in all three SDKs. Billing cannot read usage from a large terminal event. The oracle does not compare arguments for the six new kinds, and the § 5.5 rewrite does not cover most of the items it must rewrite.

## Findings

Paths: `rs/…` and `py/…` are under `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-core-sma-769/`. `base.py`, `ai.py`, `json.py` (LangChain) and `*.mjs` (openai-node) are under `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-smaschek-dev-paigasus-paigasus-core/1897327f-fffc-4b34-860d-d276c6197223/scratchpad/sdk-src/`. `_responses.py` and `_streaming.py` are in `py/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/openai/`.

### BLOCKER

- **The item class is not fixed across views for tool-free items (I1 break)** - R8 (type, id, call_id, name equality) applies only to tool-bearing items. § 5.4 says "Tool-free and provider-run items need R4 to R7, R12 and R13 only". The class is fixed at `added`, so an index that is added as `message` (or `reasoning`, or `web_search_call`) and then arrives as a `custom_tool_call` at `done`, or as a `function_call` in the terminal `response.output`, goes out unheld. Evidence from the sources:
  - LangChain makes a tool call from any `output_item.done` whose item type is `custom_tool_call`. It never checks the `added` type (`base.py:5615-5631`). Built-in kinds become content blocks the same way (`base.py:5596-5614`).
  - openai-python `ResponseStream` does not raise when the terminal item at a completed index has another identity. The `final_completed_item is not None` guard skips it (`_responses.py:484-494`), and `get_final_response()` returns the new call.
  - openai-node `#assertComplete` skips an item it cannot find (`ResponseStream.mjs:244-250`). `cloneValidatedResponse` then makes the terminal output the snapshot.
  - R12's "A `response.output` item that never streamed" can mean per index or per identity, so two builders can build it differently.
  - Event level: § 5.3 makes an item-scoped event tool-bearing or tool-free by its item, but no rule binds an event type to an item type. A `response.function_call_arguments.delta` inside a `custom_tool_call` item reaches LangChain as an extra `tool_call_chunk` at the same index. LangChain joins the args, and `parse_partial_json` keeps the first complete object (`json.py:129-145`). So the stray `{"__arg1":"rm -rf /"}` plus the decided `{"__arg1":"ls"}` runs `rm -rf /`.
  - The same event on a `message` item gives LangChain a call named `""` (`ai.py:557-561`).
  | Why it matters: All three supported parsers can run a call that no decider saw, or other arguments than the decider saw, under T2. The § 9.3 quirk list does not generate these shapes, so P1 would not find them. | Suggested fix: (1) Apply R8 to every item. The terminal item at each index has the same `type` and `id` as the streamed item, and a tool-bearing terminal item equals its `done` item. (2) Add a closed map from each item-scoped event type to its one item type. Use Node's `expectedOutputItemTypes` (`response-accumulator.mjs:111-153`), plus `content_part.*` → `message`/`reasoning` and `shell_call_command.*` → `shell_call`. A mismatch is malformed. (3) `added.item` must be an object with a string `type`. `item: null` is malformed, because both SDKs skip it (`_responses.py:432`, `ResponseStream.mjs:215`). (4) Add a generator quirk for each case.

- **D13 billing cannot read usage from a large terminal event** - `UsageScanner` skips any record over `MAX_RECORD_BYTES = 64 * 1024` and never parses it (`rs/.../paigasus-gateway/src/adapters/http/usage.rs:11`, `:122-126`). Every Responses lifecycle event carries the whole `response` object. That object holds the echoed `instructions` and `tools`, and in `response.completed` every output item again (text, arguments, encrypted reasoning). An agent with a long system prompt and many tool schemas can pass 64 KiB. I did not measure the sizes. Then `reported` stays `None`, and `ChargeGuard` charges the request estimate plus one token per record (`application/charge_guard.rs:124`). This happens with interception on or off. The fallbacks are also undefined for Responses: `non_stream_usage` reads only `choices[]` (`usage.rs:65`), and the D13 request estimate has no defined shape, but it would become the common path. | Why it matters: Large responses would be undercharged by large factors. The budget limits (AC 1) would not hold. | Suggested fix: Specify a Responses usage reader that gets `response.usage` with no 64 KiB buffer limit, for example a bounded streaming scan for the `usage` key of `response`. Add service tests with terminal events over 64 KiB and over 1 MiB. Specify the request estimate (`instructions`, `input` string, each input item type) and the body fallback (`output[].content[].text`, `arguments`) as precisely as the chat D14 rule.

- **The oracle does not compare arguments for the six new kinds** - `kind_of` maps every kind it does not list to `"other"` (`rs/.../paigasus-gateway-core/tests/support/oracle.rs:89-97`). `arguments_match` returns `true` for `"other"` (`:118-121`). § 5.1 gives Computer, LocalShell, Shell, ApplyPatch, ToolSearch and McpApprovalRequest the same decided form as Other (the raw `done` item). § 9.1 does not say how to compare them. | Why it matters: P1 cannot fail on a wrong shell command, patch diff or computer action. D15 calls these the most dangerous kinds. The proof for them would pass with nothing checked. | Suggested fix: Give each new kind its own model kind and a defined comparison. For example, compare the item as JSON with `status` removed, after the normalisation each SDK applies (LangChain uses `model_dump(exclude_none=True)`, `base.py:5612`). Add a mutation proof: a changed `action.commands` in the `done` item must make P1 fail.

### MAJOR

- **The strict envelope rules reject echoed request data** - Lifecycle events and non-stream bodies echo `text.format.schema`, `metadata`, `tools[]` (outside `parameters`) and `instructions`. Only `input`, `input_schema` and `parameters` get the data rules (`rs/.../paigasus-gateway-core/src/json.rs:105`). A structured-output property such as `"Name"`, `"ID"` or `"Type"`, a metadata key `"Id"`, or a property `constructor` makes `response.created` and `response.completed` `case_folded_key` or `prototype_key` (`json.rs:73-85`). The body path runs `check_numbers` over the whole body (`src/body.rs:36`), so a schema `"maximum": 1e300` gives `lossy_number` and a 502. | Why it matters: Common structured-output requests fail. A dropped `response.created` makes Python and Node raise at the next event. With a hold open, the failure blocks every tool call. | Suggested fix: Add per-format data subtrees for Responses: `response.text`, `response.metadata`, `response.tools`, `response.instructions` and `response.prompt`. Apply `check_numbers` only to tool-bearing items. Add fixtures. Also decide whether the new keys (`output_index`, `item_id`, `call_id`, `item`, `output`, …) join `CLASSIFIER_KEYS`. A global list would change chat behaviour (AC 8), so make it per format.

- **The record size limits break ordinary Responses traffic** - The interceptor treats a record over `max_record_bytes` (1 MiB) as a stream failure even with an empty queue (`src/interceptor.rs:234-237`). Long `instructions` repeat in `response.created`, `response.in_progress` and `response.completed`. `image_generation_call` items and `partial_image` events carry base64 images. `response.completed` repeats the whole output. | Why it matters: Every SDK then raises, because there is no `response.created` or no `response.completed`. This also happens on text-only streams. | Suggested fix: State a size model for Responses. Either use a larger cap for lifecycle events, or do not parse the `instructions`, `tools` and image `result` subtrees. Add a test above 1 MiB. Also review `max_request_bytes` (1 MiB default, `paigasus-gateway/src/config.rs:438`). D3 makes clients resend the whole conversation, with encrypted reasoning, on every turn.

- **The § 5.5 rewrite does not cover most blocked items** - The rewrite has five gaps:
  - "A blocked item always has at least three frames" is false. The 3.48.0 union has no progress event for `computer_call`, `apply_patch_call`, `local_shell_call`, `mcp_approval_request` or `tool_search_call`. With R5 and R13, their only frames are `added` and `done` (k = 2). With k = 2, strictly increasing numbers for four events are impossible.
  - Some items are blocked while they assemble: on `HoldLimit`, on a stream failure, or when a hold opens in `Mode::Failed` (`interceptor.rs:285-291`). Their frames are released one by one, and the spec defines no events for this case.
  - A truncated item has no `done` frame.
  - In the k = 3 case, LangChain never sees the notice. LangChain reads text only from `output_text.delta` (`base.py:5492`).
  - For a truncated item, R12 ("equals the done item") cannot hold. The terminal event then becomes a deviation and is dropped instead of rewritten.
  | Why it matters: An implementer must invent the common case. A wrong choice makes Node raise or drops the terminal event. | Suggested fix: Define the rewrite per frame:
  - The item's `added` frame becomes the replacement `added`, `content_part.added` and `output_text.delta`.
  - The middle frames are dropped.
  - The item's `done` frame becomes the replacement `done`. When no `done` arrives, synthesize one before the terminal event, `[DONE]`, EOF or the D12 frame, as chat's `closing()` does.
  - Always replace the terminal item at a blocked index, and exempt it from R12.
  - Drop the strict sequence rule, or allow repeated numbers. No SDK reads `sequence_number` for `create`.
  - Give the exact JSON of each event: `item_id`, `output_index`, `content_index: 0`, `logprobs: []` and `annotations: []`. Node raises when `item_id` is missing (`response-accumulator.mjs:201-208`).

- **R11 contradicts itself for `shell_call`, and assumes built-ins are complete at `added`** - R11 requires `added` = `done` except `status`, and it also allows `response.shell_call_command.*`. Node builds `action.commands` from those events, starting from the `added` item (`response-accumulator.mjs:664-683`). So a streamed shell call has different `action.commands` in `added` and `done`. "Their concatenated text" is ambiguous: `commands` is an array keyed by `command_index`, and those events have no `item_id`. Nothing measures whether `apply_patch_call` or `computer_call` arrive complete at `added`. | Why it matters: R11 either blocks every streamed shell call, or implementers guess. If the `added` items are partial, R11 blocks every apply_patch and computer call. | Suggested fix: State the rule per command index: `added.command` plus the deltas equal `done.command`, which equals `done.item.action.commands[i]`, and indexes append in order. Leave `action.commands` out of the `added` = `done` comparison. Add a measurement of the `added` and `done` shapes of each client-run built-in kind.

- **The recordings cannot test the rules that real traffic may break** - § 9.4 records functions, custom tools, reasoning and text only. Nothing records built-in or provider-run tools, a long reasoning run (keepalives), a `max_output_tokens` cut inside a call, `response.failed`, an `error` event, a terminal event over 64 KiB, or structured output. LangChain's source says that real traffic breaks R4/R6: "After several built-in tool calls the API can report a later `output_index` on an item's `done` events than on its `added` event" (`base.py:5419-5421`).   - A `keepalive` without `sequence_number` fails R7 ("every event has it or none").

  - A `[DONE]` after the terminal event is dropped as `after_done`, which reds `recorded_streams_pass_unchanged`.
  | Why it matters: A deviation sets `Mode::Failed`, which blocks every later hold in the stream. Long reasoning streams with gpt-6.1-sol, the target of § 1, are the most exposed. | Suggested fix: Add these scenarios to `capture.py` and to the M-list. Exempt `keepalive` and `error` from R1 and R7, or measure them first. Define what happens to `[DONE]` after a terminal event.

- **The next turn after a rewrite is not measured** - Under D3 the client sends the rewritten output back as `input`. In a reasoning model's output, a `reasoning` item often comes directly before the `function_call`. After the rewrite, `msg_paigasus_<i>` follows that reasoning item instead. I recall a known OpenAI 400 for a reasoning item "provided without its required following item", but this is not measured here. The `msg_paigasus_` id might also fail OpenAI's input id checks. | Why it matters: If OpenAI rejects it, every block breaks the agent loop on the next turn, for exactly the models of § 1. | Suggested fix: Add a measurement that replays a rewritten output as `input`, with and without `store`, with `encrypted_content`. Settle the rewrite before implementation. One option is to also drop the preceding `reasoning` item.

- **`ToolCall` drops identity fields that clients dispatch on** - `function_call` has `namespace`, `caller` and `async` (`types/responses/response_function_tool_call.py:50-57`). openai-python finds the tool by `(namespace, name)` (`lib/_parsing/_responses.py:170-189`). Compare them in R8 and in the oracle. Read `namespace` tools into `TurnFacts.definitions`.

- **`TurnFacts.definitions` can be incomplete in the way D3 gives as a reason to refuse `prompt`** - D3 refuses `prompt` because a template "can add tools that the gateway cannot see". `tool_search` (deferred tools, `tool_search_output`) and `additional_tools` items add tools inside a stateless request too. | Why it matters: The reasoning is not consistent. Definition-based policies fail open or closed, with no rule to say which. | Suggested fix: Mark the turn as having incomplete definitions when these tools are used, or read `additional_tools`/`tool_search_output` as definitions. State the rule.

- **The client models do not count everything a client runs** - The models have five gaps:

  - `runners()` falls back to the chat runners with `_ =>` (`oracle.rs:81-85`). If the Responses arm is missing, the tests run with zero calls and pass.
  | Why it matters: P1 can pass while a client runs a call. | Suggested fix: Extend the models and add a raw-stream model. Match by `position` and `call_id` too, or remove "output index" from I1. Make the wildcard arm panic. Add the missing quirks: an item type change, an event on the wrong item type, a duplicate `id` or `call_id`, `item: null`, a top-level `error` key, `[DONE]x`, and a non-empty `in_progress.output`.
